#2882. Nick Sirianni admits that he misled reporters about quarterback situation

How do you know when a football coach is lying? If he’s good at it, you don’t.

Because they all do. Particularly in so-called “must-lie” situations.

There’s an art to it. A way to conceal a lie with another lie. On Friday, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni opted not to lie about the fact that he lied on Monday when he told reporters that quarterback Tanner McKee would not be benched.

“Tanner’s our guy,” Sirianni said. “We’re not making any changes there.”

On Wednesday, the Eagles made a change there, elevating Joe Milton over McKee. The move was announced after Sirianni had his midweek media availability, which prevented him from being asked questions about the change in position from “Tanner’s our guy” to “Tanner’s not our guy.”

On Friday, Sirianni finally faced the music regarding his comments from Monday. In lieu of coming up with an explanation premised on the idea that what he said was true when he said it and circumstances changed, Sirianni surprisingly admitted that he wasn’t telling the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth to reporters and, in turn, the fans.

“I was going to hold onto that as long as I possibly could, every second, every minute,” Sirianni said. “Again, I’m not real shy with you guys. I’m going to tell you what I want to tell you guys. I respect the job that y’all have to do, but I’m going to tell you what I want to tell you guys because I’m always going to protect the team first and foremost.

“Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold onto information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game. I know there’s a lot of interest in everything that you all want to hear, the fans want to hear. My job is to win football games, do everything we can do to help win football games, protect the guys here on this football team, and handle everything that I can inside.”

In an industry where the truth is only told when it’s coincidental to strategic interests, it’s jarring that Sirianni told the truth that he was lying. It would have been easy to say, “We took a more careful look at the situation after Monday.” Or, even more simply, “We changed our mind. Shit happens.”

Instead, Sirianni opted to say, essentially, “Bullshit happens.” Instead of bothering to concoct a cover story regarding his lie, he said, essentially, “Yeah. I lied. I’ll do it whenever I feel like I have to.”

That’s the most important thing to remember. Coaches lie whenever they feel like they have to. Despite that fact, reporters and fans routinely take their words at face value, swallowing the bullshit while saying, “Thank you, sir, may I have another?”

So thank you, Nick, for making my job a little easier. In my first week of law school, one of the professors said, “The most important thing I can do for you is to give you a good crap filter.”

Because crap is everywhere. Usually, the people spewing it don’t admit it. When they do, it provides a tangible reminder as to whatever they say in the future.

For Sirianni, that’s the most problematic aspect of his decision to tell the truth about lying. There’s now an “Exhibit A” to which anyone and everyone can point as to anything and everything he says when assessing whether he’s being straight with reporters and, in turn, with fans.

#2880. Luka vs Blazers, Wemby and more: 5 NBA Cup games to watch

The second batch of NBA Cup group play games takes place Friday, Nov. 6, with nine games on the schedule.

The slate includes several heavyweight matchups, led by the Los Angeles Lakers hosting the Western Conference-leading Portland Trail Blazers in a rematch of the Blazers' 136-129 win on Oct. 27. The defending conference champion San Antonio Spurs also look to maintain their strong start against the Sacramento Kings.

In the East, the conference-leading Philadelphia 76ers visit the Cleveland Cavaliers, while the Washington Wizards and Atlanta Hawks open the evening's NBA Cup action.

MORE: Who is making a run at Doncic, Wembanyama? Latest NBA MVP rankings

The Luka Doncic train keeps rolling. He enters Friday averaging an NBA-best 38.5 points and has scored 40 or more five times in eight games. But the Western Conference-leading Trail Blazers have won three in a row without Ja Morant and already beat the Lakers 136-129 on Oct. 27.

Can Victor Wembanyama possibly top his 52-point, 24-rebound performance in his last outing against the Dallas Mavericks? It's possible against the 1-7 Kings, who ranked 28th in defensive efficiency.

Oklahoma City has surprised despite a rash of devastating injuries, but must contain Grizzlies guard Ty Jerome, who has become a walking bucket during the first couple weeks of the season, with two 40-point games to his credit.

A possible Eastern Conference final matchup as Cleveland looks for revenge after blowing a 29-point lead to Philadelphia on Oct. 22. The 76ers have three 20-points-per-game scorers and have gotten off to an 8-1 start.

The Celtics have done just fine without Jaylen Brown, as Paul George has picked up the scoring slack in a formidable duo with Jayson Tatum. The Hornets have struggled, losing their past five games and are the only team in the league that doesn't average 100 points a game.

Each NBA Cup game also counts toward the regular-season standings, except for the championship game on Dec. 11. Teams play each of their four group opponents once, with the results determining who advances to the knockout rounds.

#2874. ‘He doesn’t necessarily have a super-high IQ’: Doc Rivers slams Giannis Antetokounmpo

Former Milwaukee Bucks coach Doc Rivers officially stepped down as head coach in April after a long NBA tenure. Shortly after, longtime Bucks forward Giannis Antetokounmpo was traded to the Miami Heat to embark on the back half of his career.

Already nine games into the regular season, the Heat hold a 3-6 record as Antetokounmpo averages 27.3 points per game, 12.7 rebounds, and 5.6 assists to lead the team in both points and rebounds, a role he is very familiar with. But even as part of a new team and new system, it looks like we're seeing a repeat of the days in Milwaukee, with the G-man putting on a show and the team struggling to execute.

Recently, Rivers sat with Bill Simmons on The Bill Simmons Podcast to address some of his grievances with Antetokounmpo and the highs and lows of coaching during their time in Milwaukee.

"He's not easy. Because he plays at this crazy downhill pace. He's really a difficult guy," Rivers said in a clip shared by Ahmed/The Ears on X. "He has this great passing ability, but he doesn't necessarily have a super-high IQ at the same time. It's really a strange thing, and he really has only one way: downhill, force, force. Every play, he wants to force it."

"I wish he'd learned how to execute better. He's one of those guys you get a lot of them from the US, AAU guys that have never needed to execute because they can do it on their own. But that doesn't help the team," Rivers continued.

"The thing he needs to still learn is the value of execution, how important it is, when you're in practice and at shootaround, to lock in on execution. Now he has a coach who's as good as there is in execution," he added.

Simmons interjected, giving the Greek Freak the benefit of the doubt for being one of the most athletically talented players remaining in the NBA; sometimes being aggressive works.

"Yeah, but that's good for him, and what a lot of players don't understand is, 'Yeah, I don't need that, I can do that.' Yeah, you can, but for the team to work, you have to learn how to execute," Rivers added.

Rivers was officially inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in August, and since stepping down from coaching has taken up a role with NBC Sports as an NBA game analyst for the 2026-27 season. With the season just beginning, Antetokounmpo has plenty of time to get adjusted to Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra's methods, as he is not shy about execution or winning.

Williams isn't a high-upside option, but he has been very consistent so far this year and should be a safe streaming option.

#2871. Brandon Aiyuk plans to meet with 49ers at team's business offices, not team facility

49ers tight end George Kittle was right, sort of. Receiver Brandon Aiyuk won’t “get in” the team facility on Friday, because he’s not trying to.

Per agent Drew Rosenhaus, Friday’s meeting will happen at the team’s business offices and not at the team’s practice facility.

That makes the session not a formal reporting-for-duty by Aiyuk, in the hopes of forcing the team’s hand. As explained earlier today, the NFL still hasn’t reinstated Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list — even though Rosenhaus filed the request on October 27.

Instead, it’s a meeting presumably aimed at negotiating a resolution to the situation.

The 49ers pushed to reporters on Thursday night the idea that Aiyuk’s return to the NFL is tied to the $13 million the team believes he owes in previously paid signing bonus. That shouldn’t be part of the analysis as to whether he’s reinstated by the league, whether the 49ers put him on the roster again, and/or whether the 49ers cut him.

But they’re making it an issue, because they can tie his ability to play to his willingness to wire the disputed funds to the team.

So that’s what’s happening. The brakes already have been applied to what should have been an administrative and automatic process. The league and the 49ers are working together to help the team get money back from Aiyuk before Aiyuk is permitted to get back into the league.

Then there’s the fact that an active arrest warrant is pending for Aiyuk, arising from a speeding incident. The business meeting could potentially be interrupted by an attempt to enforce a specific item of police business.

#2870. In-form Thierno Barry leads Everton to a 3-1 victory over Coventry

Somewhat prophetically boss David Moyes, equalling Harry Catterick's record of 592 matches in charge, had said at his pre-match press conference that "Erling Haaland should be worried."

And while realistically the Norway international will not be losing any sleep at the thought, Barry's form as the club's only recognized striker is proving a major boost.

With Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall chipping in with goals from midfield, scoring the third nine minutes from time, to add to his all-round creativity Moyes is squeezing everything out of his limited resources.

#2869. How the 49ers plan to use DeForest Buckner with new look DL room

The San Francisco 49ers are hitting the field on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders, coming off a bye week, and they'll have their new addition on the defensive line with them. Recently traded defensive tackle DeForest Buckner is set to make his 49ers return, marking his first game in San Francisco uniform since the 2019 Super Bowl.

Buckner, 32, has long been known as a quality pass rusher with a unique size-length profile at 6'7, and will hope to add some of that to a young defensive tackle room that also includes Osa Odighizuwa. Now, the 49ers have their two veterans, along with rookie Gracen Halton and former undrafted free agent Sebastian Valdez as their top depth.

With the Indianapolis Colts, Buckner had a top five snap count among defensive tackles this season. With the 49ers, that'll hopefully drop as the 49ers rotate their linemen more. But, with Buckner and Odighizuwa both having familiarity playing as three-techniques, how will the 49ers use Buckner in his return?

"We've done so many different things, moved people around," defensive coordinator Raheem Morris said. "They have the ability to play three-technique. They have the ability to play nose. They have the ability to play four-eye, the ability to play on the edge. You've kind of seen these guys kind of move around all over the place, so I wouldn't really put them in a bucket.

"You're talking about a guy with supreme talent. Those guys kind of can do whatever you ask them to do. Traditionally he's been a three-technique around here, playing a huge role and doing some really good things. He'll do a lot of the same thing. I'm a big believer in doing what people do really well and we'll try to find out what he does really well again, implement them to what the guys have been doing and put those guys together and put them out there playing fast."

The 49ers have regularly been moving players around, kicking some of their bigger edges inside, while also creating different ways to rush the passer. The creativity should increase with Nick Bosa also trending to play, but it doesn't seem like Morris is concerned with the usage.

San Francisco has been without Bosa for a few weeks now, and their pass rush has struggled a bit as a result. Now, with him and Buckner both likely in the fold this week, what will that do for the defense?

"I don't know when it would be a bad time to get a guy like Buck," Morris added. "It's been a lot of fun to meet him the last couple of days and be around him and watch him practice and put him a part of it. Really feel like I'm further away from it than he is because of how long he spent here and the time that he spent here and how much he means to this organization and the people around him.

"So, it's been a lot of fun being around that guy and to have that whole unit being able to come back relatively healthy. To see these guys (Buckner and Bosa) probably for the first time altogether, I think altogether, for the first time this year, I think it'd be a lot of fun."

Now, the 49ers have two veterans in their defensive tackle room, which should only help in the development of younger guys like Mykel Williams, Halton, Valdez, Romello Height, and the rest of the room.

"Buck's done it at a very high level for such a long time," Morris continued. "I don't know if there's anybody in this building that can't pick something up from him. I just know how much, let's just go with the ultimate leader in Fred [Warner] and [Dre] Greenlaw, how much respect those guys have for him. So when you're talking about guys that have done a lot of really cool things at different positions that can learn from him, you can only imagine what the guys up front can get from him, just those guys being together.

"Having Osa being a vet and then having Buck come in with some different perspective, different realities of what he's been through and what he's done. To be able to come back into the fold and really pick it back up and fit right back in with the guy that's coached him, guys that he's familiar with, whether it be the head coach or his position coach, I think is always a really good thing."

The Niners will kick things off against the Raiders this weekend as they look to start the second half of the season hot. We'll get to see how Buckner looks returning to the 49ers, and whether the team still needs to make another move ahead of the deadline.

#2868. Steph Curry earns ‘healthy monetary value’ from Klay Thompson

"There was a healthy monetary value to that," Curry quipped after Golden State's 120-100 win.

Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry, left, talks with Miami Heat guard Klay Thompson after an NBA game Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, in San Francisco. AP Photo/Tony Avelar

Thompson confirmed that he most definitely heard from Curry after his Cougars took a 76-61 home loss to the Wildcats. In fact, that was all he heard leading into their own showdown.

Stephen Curry (30) of the Golden State Warriors handles the ball against Klay Thompson (11) of the Miami Heat on Nov. 5, 2026, at Chase Center in San Francisco. NBAE via Getty Images

Thompson, averaging 24.7 over his previous three games, was contained to 11 points on 3-of-10 shooting. He had been 19-for-36 from 3 over his past three games but drained only two of his seven attempts from distance, including an air ball on his contested first heave.

In a twist on their previous matchups, the old Splash Brothers ended up defending each other for a good portion of the game. Thompson drained one of his 3s on Curry and picked up another three points at the foul line after getting Curry to bite on a pump fake.

Klay Thompson #11 of the Miami Heat shoots against Stephen Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors in San Francisco on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. Getty Images

"It's still surreal playing against him," Curry said. "It's always gonna be that way cause we've gone through so many battles together. And it's kind of cool even at this stage to guard him.

"You've been on the other side of it for so long, so there's an appreciation there. I think mostly it's just an excitement of the fact that we're still able to have battles. You know that every one that you get is one closer to the end. So you try to appreciate it even though there's definitely a competitive spirit out there."

Stephen Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors and Klay Thompson #11 of the Miami Heat look on during a game, Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, in San Francisco. NBAE via Getty Images

Still, the loss could only sour the night so much.

"It still feels special every time," Thompson said after his fifth trip back, "especially receiving the love from the fanbase and seeing people that I spent years with. It'll always feel like home. …

"It was fun, really fun. Steph's super crafty, still to this day. It felt good to block his shot. He made a great up and under on me. He had an incredible night."

Thompson lamented Miami's tough travel schedule, playing at Golden State a night after knocking off the Clippers in double overtime. Thompson's corner 3 at the buzzer sealed the win.

Stephen Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors and Klay Thompson #11 of the Miami Heat look on during a game at Chase Center in San Francisco on Nov. 5, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images

Warriors coach Steve Kerr said that he had been watching live.

"I texted Draymond [Green] right after," Curry said. "Just told him Killa Klay. It's always great to see him having fun but then you obviously wanted to come in and shut his water off tonight."

#2867. Eagles Film Review: Joe Milton is an easy player to get excited about

This week got away from me. Life has been ridiculously busy, and I couldn't put together my usual weekly preview article. But with the Eagles turning to Joe Milton at quarterback, I still wanted to give you something. So, let's do this! Milton is an easy player to get excited about and a lot of fun to watch. I enjoyed this one.

The first thing you notice is the arm. Milton can rifle short and intermediate throws without needing a big wind-up or much of a step into the ball. It almost looks like a flick of the wrist, and the ball arrives with unusual zip. The release is quick, too. He does not need a long gathering motion to generate velocity, which matters when a defender is closing or when the offense wants the ball out before the underneath coverage can rally.

That quick release could also make the Eagles' RPO game more dangerous. A bubble or slant has to get out before the defender responsible for the receiver can drive downhill. Milton has the arm to deliver those throws quickly, and the ball can arrive before the defense has time to recover. The speed of the delivery gives the concept a chance to punish a defense for overcommitting to the run.

Receivers may need to adjust, because the ball comes in hot, but this is a rare physical tool. It jumps out on film. The same velocity that makes an RPO throw difficult to defend can also make an ordinary catch harder if the ball is high or behind the receiver.

The arm also lets Milton challenge tight windows. On this rep, he sees the linebacker dropping underneath and trusts that he can beat him to the spot. The ball gets there with enough speed to take away the defender's chance to close the space.

That is the frustrating part of his film. His accuracy is not uniformly bad. He can put the ball exactly where it needs to go, then miss the next one by a mile.

Milton can drive the ball downfield, too. The Eagles have been short on vertical passing lately, and this preseason throw shows why they should give him chances to attack deep. He drops the ball into the bucket with both velocity and placement. This isn't just about throwing it far; he has to put enough air and location on it for the receiver to run onto the ball while keeping the defender from making a play.

A strong arm can force a defense to respect the deep part of the field, but a deep passing game only works if the quarterback can pair range with precise ball location. Milton shows that combination here. The Eagles have not given us much vertical offense recently, and I need to see some of it. I'm hopeful Milton will throw some deep bombs this week!

Comfortable on the move and patient in the pocket

I expect the Eagles to use more play-action bootlegs with Milton. He looked comfortable throwing on the move throughout the preseason, and this was supposed to be a bigger part of the offense already. Boot action can make the defense honor the run, change the quarterback's launch point, and create a simpler picture outside the pocket. Milton can sell that action and still deliver the ball while moving, which gives the play a chance to stress the edge defender and the coverage behind him.

If the Eagles want to lean on play action, Milton's comfort on the move is a real reason to call it. Maybe we finally see more of it this week. If you can't run play-action bootlegs with Joe Milton, I'm not sure you will be able to do it with anyone…

Milton can run, but he does not seem eager to abandon the pocket at the first opportunity. Here, he eliminates the routes at the top of the screen, works back to the comeback, steps up to avoid the edge rusher, and keeps looking to throw. He could take off through the open lane, but he wants to win as a passer first. He is prepared to stay in the pocket, make space for the throw, and keep his eyes downfield.

He is particularly comfortable rolling to his left. This is a 25-yard completion on the move, and he makes it look easy. A right-handed quarterback throwing across his body in that direction can make the ball sail, but Milton stays balanced enough to put it on the receiver without stopping and resetting. He gets the throw away while still moving rather than needing to gather himself and give the defense extra time to close.

Throwing on the move while rolling to the left, for a right-handed quarterback, is one of the more difficult skills to execute. Milton can do it pretty easily. The Eagles can move him away from the original launch point without reducing the play to "run or throw it away." The film shows that he can keep the play alive as a passer.

Then there is the deep ball. On this 50-yard throw, Milton looks off the safety, takes the one-on-one shot, and puts the ball in the back corner of the end zone. He may be a beat late, but the arm strength gives him enough margin to complete a throw that would be unavailable to many quarterbacks. He has to get it over the coverage and still keep it in a spot where only his receiver can make the play.

The running ability is another obvious way to make this offense more interesting. Milton is a big, powerful quarterback who can move quickly in the open field. The 4.6 40 time is evident on film. The Eagles should design runs for him and use that threat to help the run game. If they cannot get a quarterback with his size and speed to create something on the ground, I am not sure what else they are waiting for.

I want to see some QB counter bash, QB draw, and good old-fashioned read-option runs. Those concepts make the defense account for Milton as a ball carrier instead of treating him as a passer who might scramble only when the play breaks down. On a read option, the edge defender has to respect the quarterback keep; on a designed draw or counter bash, Milton can become an extra runner in the blocking scheme. That can change the numbers in the box and create a conflict for the defense. It will not fix a struggling run game by itself, but it gives the Eagles another way to make the defense hesitate.

The biggest issue is inconsistent accuracy. Milton doesn't always miss by a little; when he does, the ball can be nowhere near the target. This is a wide-open deep crossing route with a clean pocket, and he sails it badly. There is no pressure forcing him to rush the throw in this example, and the receiver has room to work across the field. The ball simply does not give him a chance to complete it.

The arm strength makes the good throws spectacular, but you can't miss like this and play in this league. There is a reason a quarterback with this level of physical talent was available. He will miss some throws by a big distance.

The other obvious risk is that Milton trusts his arm enough to force throws that are not there. He can fit the ball into windows other quarterbacks cannot, but that confidence can turn into a turnover when the read or timing is wrong.

The Eagles have leaned toward a risk-averse style; I am not sure they can play exactly the same way with Milton. He is a boom-or-bust quarterback, and the coaching staff will have to accept some lows if it wants to access the highs. There is a balance to find: let him use the arm and create explosive plays, while giving him clear answers so he does not feel he has to force a hero throw on every difficult down.

I am not pretending Milton is a polished answer at quarterback. Obviously. The accuracy can be wildly inconsistent, and the bad plays are pretty rough. But there is legitimate talent here. He has a quick release, rare velocity, real downfield ability, and enough mobility to add a different dimension to the offense. The Eagles have spent too much of this season making the offense hard to watch. Milton gives them a chance to run more boot action, take vertical shots, and use the quarterback in the run game.

Will it be messy? Almost certainly. It could completely suck, let's be honest. This is a poorly schemed offense with a lot of talent issues right now. If they allow loads of unblocked pressure again, he probably won't have a chance to succeed. Milton's mobility may help him escape some of that pressure. But the protection and the play design still have to give him a chance to operate.

But if the Eagles cannot be good right now, I would at least like them to be fun. Why the hell not? Let Milton rip it. I've been so bored with the Eagles since Jalen Hurts has been unable to play. Joe Milton might just make it a little bit more fun, just not necessarily better.

Thank you for reading! I'd love to hear your thoughts, so feel free to comment below and ask any questions. If you would like to support me further, please check out my Patreon here!

#2865. Yahoo Perfect 5: Luka Dončić, Evan Mobley and Walker Kessler lead my Friday lineup

Yahoo Sports is giving fans another way to play fantasy basketball with Perfect 5, a free-to-play game featuring each week's NBA on Prime doubleheader. The rules are simple: pick five players, stay within a $15 budget and rack up fantasy points through scoring, rebounds, assists, defensive stats and 3s.

Friday's slate features the 76ers at Cavaliers (7:30 p.m. ET) and Trail Blazers at Lakers (10 p.m. ET). There's plenty of star power, but the key to building a competitive lineup is finding the right matchups and the values in the $1 tier.

Using RotoWire's data and Yahoo projections, I ran 20,000 simulations of the slate. I'm paying up for Luka Dončić and leaning on two $4 bigs with great setups. Here's my lineup:

In my sims, this group averaged 160.08 fantasy points and finished in the top 1% of the field 21.7% of the time, the best rate of any lineup I tested.

Luka Dončić – PG, Los Angeles Lakers – ($5, 76% picked)

The chalkiest pick in the pool feels necessary because he's been one of the best, if not the best, players to start the season. Dončić is averaging 38.5 points, 8.2 rebounds, 8.0 assists and 5.9 3s, and he's gone for 40+ points in three straight games. Portland is middle of the pack against point guards, but when a guy is as hot as Luka, with a usage rate north of 40%, you play 'em.

He was in the single best lineup in 55% of my simulations, more than any other player. Portland beat the Lakers 136-129 in L.A. on Oct. 27, even though Luka went for 41 points, 9 assists and 6 3s. He'll want this one back. Lock him in.

Evan Mobley – PF, Cleveland Cavaliers – ($4, 12% picked)

Mobley is projected for 42.46 fantasy points at $4, within about a point of Donovan Mitchell, whose salary is $5. He's putting up 18.8 points, 8.2 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.3 blocks, while hitting 2.1 3s a night. The matchup is neutral (Philly ranks 19th in fantasy points allowed to power forwards), and his usage has ticked up to 23.6% over the last three games.

Jarrett Allen is questionable with a right knee contusion, after leaving Monday's contest after just seven minutes. If Allen sits, Mobley soaks up even more of the paint work against a light Philly frontcourt. At 12% picked, he's still the best combination of value and leverage on the slate.

Walker Kessler – C, Los Angeles Lakers – ($4, 12% picked)

Portland gives up 60.4 fantasy points per game to centers, the second-most in the league and about eight more than average. He's putting up 14.4 points, 10.2 rebounds and 2.7 blocks per night. I originally had Deni Avdija in this spot, but the matchups flipped it. The Lakers are one of the toughest defenses against small forwards, while Kessler gets one of the league's softest frontcourts. Now Kessler grades out better, and he's picked at the same 12% rate. Avdija is still a fine pivot if you'd rather have his playmaking, and that version of this lineup was a close second.

Sidy Cissoko – SF, Portland Trail Blazers – ($1, 41% picked)

Cissoko is the most popular non-Luka pick on the board. He's projected for 17.58 fantasy points at a $1 salary; I think he might be the best points-per-dollar mark on the slate. While the matchup isn't great (the Lakers are 26th in fantasy points allowed to small forwards), his minutes have held to around 21 a night. Trusting the math here, as he showed up in the optimal lineup in 45% of my sims.

Meleek Thomas – SG, Cleveland Cavaliers – ($1, 14% picked)

Here's where I'm going against Yahoo projections. Thomas is projected for only 12.00 fantasy points: that's too low. Over the last three contests, he's averaging 13.0 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.0 assist and 2.6 3s, which works out to roughly 21 fantasy points. His minutes match his production: he played 22.3 minutes over that span with a 25.4% usage rate.

He was listed with right foot soreness on a recent injury report, so give it a look before tip. I'd originally pegged Kentavious Caldwell-Pope as the safe swap, but his minutes have dropped to 21, 13 and 18 in his last three, so I'm sticking with Thomas.

Not quite. Using Yahoo's projections, the highest-scoring possible lineup is Dončić, Mobley, Jaylen Brown, Cissoko and Caldwell-Pope at 163.64 fantasy points. Mine comes in 3.56 points behind it.

The max lineup is a good build. It averaged nearly 164.0 points in my sims and finished in the top 1% about 13% of the time. Brown is a strong play, since Cleveland gives up the fifth-most fantasy points to small forwards. The weak spot is Caldwell-Pope and his shrinking minutes. The other problem is that everyone reading the same projections gets to this exact five, and it's the chalkiest high-projection build. In a game where you're trying to finish top-three against the whole Yahoo community, tying a bunch of people doesn't help much. Swapping Brown for Kessler and Caldwell-Pope for Thomas gives up 3.56 projected points but buys better matchups and more separation.

You can start building your Perfect 5 roster for Friday's slate now, including going up against me in my Perfect 5 group. Good luck!

#2863. Slick Saints beat Prem Rugby Cup holders Leicester

Northampton kept their hopes of reaching the Prem Rugby Cup semi-finals alive after a dominant 39-19 derby victory over East Midlands rivals Leicester.

A youthful Saints line-up turned on the style to sink the holders at Franklin's Gardens and stretch Northampton's run to 16 successive home wins in all competitions.

Wings Tom Rowe and Amena Caqusau and full-back James Martin all touched down twice in a seven-try romp for the Saints.

After three successive defeats in the Prem Rugby Cup, last season's winners Leicester are bottom of Pool B.

It was not a perfect evening for Northampton. Already without two injured scrum-halves in England international Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland, the Saints lost a third in the 29th minute in Jonny Weimann.

The 20-year-old, made captain for the evening, limped off after creating Northampton's first two tries, number one in the 11th minute with a glorious long pass to Martin and number two five minutes later with a cross-kick to Rowe.

But England Under-18s scrum-half Sonny Goode showed Northampton's remarkable depth in the position with an impressive showing off the bench.

After being steamrollered in a feisty Prem meeting at Mattioli Woods Welford Road a fortnight ago, this emphatic win provided a measure of revenge.

Saints led 27-7 at the break with Rowe, Caqusau and centre Toby Thame also crossing.

Caqusau produced a fine finish to secure the bonus point for Saints in the 36th minute and Rowe's second on the stroke of half-time gave Saints their 20-point interval advantage.

But Martin went over for his second from a cross-kick in the 46th minute and then Caqusau added his second after some fine approach play by Goode with Leicester wing Adam Radwan in the sin-bin.

Leicester, well beaten, managed three tries, two from hooker Sam Moli and one from back row Osian Thomas.

Sale Sharks went to the top of Pool A with a tense 21-19 win over Bristol Bears at the CorpAcq Stadium.

Two tries from Arron Reed - playing at full-back - and one from Alex Wills did the damage but Bristol took the game to the wire with two tries from Max Pepper after Totoa Auvaa, the Samoan hooker given a second chance by director of rugby Pat Lam following his sacking by Saracens for his off-field conduct, had opened their account.

Sam Worsley had a chance to win it for the Bears four minutes from time but was short with a long-range penalty attempt.

#2861. The Knicks have a bench guard conundrum

When you're the defending champions, there are not many holistic things to complain about.

Sure, the Knicks started 0-3 with a very unsettling offense, but all they needed was their medicine (the Nets and Bulls) to get back to .500?

Worried about losing to Philadelphia twice in October? Joel Embiid's plantar fasciitis has already acted up; calm down.

Any "problems" this early in the season are either short-term, regarding the looming extension talks, or good problems, which are more conundrums than actual problems.

The biggest of those conundrums has to do with the Knicks' rotation, specifically with their copious amounts of guard depth.

Jalen Brunson is the head of the snake, but after him? There are a lot of players with minutes who could fluctuate on any given night.

Tyler Kolek and Jose Alvarado duel over backup ball-handler minutes. Jordan Clarkson and Deuce McBride grapple over bench two-guard minutes. Landry Shamet's strong play is actively pushing starters Mikal Bridges and Josh Hart over their minutes with the three entrenched parts of the team's nucleus.

It does qualify as a good problem to have, as injuries will undoubtedly give each of these guys ample opportunity over the course of 82 games, but when they're all healthy, like they are right now? It probably gives Mike Brown a bigger headache than watching Andre Drummond attempt layups.

All of these guys provide something that the Knicks could use more of, but have warts that can limit their playing time.

Kolek is the best true playmaker, but he's a poor defender, and his jump shot has been consistent throughout his young NBA career. This basically also describes Alvarado, but the defense is better from the New York native.

McBride has stretches where he's the team's best rate shooter and is a tremendously pesky point-of-attack defender… but is that not what the team is getting out of a taller two-guard in Shamet?

Clarkson has been a sparkplug every game he's played this year, but the 35-year-old showed his maddening inconsistency in his first year in New York.

It's created an extremely volatile rotation, which isn't surprising when you have a coach who opened the year saying only five players on this team have minutes that are secured.

Despite zero Knicks players averaging more than 33 minutes a game except Brunson (who's at 34.1), only Shamet is averaging more than 18 minutes a game off the bench.

McBride is at 17.5, Kolek is at 12.2, Alvarado is at 11.3, and Clarkson is at 9.9, but even these are deceiving.

Kolek has played steady rotation minutes, but didn't play at all in the first two games before Alvarado's ankle injury. Alvarado played 16 and 11 minutes, got hurt, got benched after nine minutes on Monday, and was on track to be a DNP-CD against the Bulls on Wednesday.

Clarkson's gone from playing three, five, or eight minutes to his spurts of 15 and 17 in the two games against the Bulls and his 11 to spark the incredible fourth quarter against Brooklyn.

McBride, who's served as the Knicks' sixth man for over two years now, has topped 17 minutes just twice. He played a season-low 11 minutes on Wednesday and hasn't had a clear role.

To get these guys more minutes, it would mean cutting minutes from Hart or Bridges. While both have their warts, and the latter continues to look somehow less involved than he was during his lowest moments last season, some of the Knicks' best lineups are coming with them on the court… just separated.

We've seen Brown deploy line changes significantly more in the early going, opting to sub in three or four players at a time to deploy uniform units, but that's not helping how erratic this all feels.

The depth is making players redundant on the court, especially with how unwise it is to run four-guard lineups in an NBA that's prioritizing size and length more and more.

And with the Knicks' extremely shallow forward and center depth? This glut might have to be sorted out at the trade deadline. As much as McBride has shown his tremendous value to the Knicks over the course of his contract, if he isn't going to play more, is it even a net positive to keep him for the playoff run?

#2860. "It's going to be amazing" – Campbell on Dortmund return

Signal Iduna Park was home for Cole Campbell for four years, but on Saturday, the American will be on the opposite side. The forward left Borussia Dortmund for newly-promoted Elversberg in the summer, where he has hit the ground running.

"I’ve had confidence in what I can do, and I am very grateful that Elversberg has put the trust in me and given me the confidence back," said Campbell in an interview with the DFL. "It’s been amazing to be here and to feel the trust and confidence that they have in me, so I am very happy to be here."

Campbell scored his first Bundesliga goal in Elversberg's opener, a surprise 3-2 win over Bayer Leverkusen. Since then, he's been moved to more of a bench role, partially due to injuries and partially to the emergence of other Elversberg attackers, like Maurice Krattenmacher.

Still, Campbell has made an impact when he's played. He scored with an acrobatic kick against Mainz to clinch a 4-1 win, taking Elversberg up to seventh in the Bundesliga. It was just his second top-flight goal.

“It was an amazing feeling for me to score a goal like this,” said Campbell. "I was very happy after the game and was also happy to have helped the team secure the win."

Campbell was only 18 when he made his debut in the Champions League, coming off the bench in front of a packed stadium against Sturm Graz. He replaced Jamie Gittens as Dortmund, then led by Nuri Şahin, snatched a dramatic 1-0 win at the death.

“At that point, it was probably one of my best feelings, and it was a dream come true to make my debut in the Champions League,” said Campbell. "To play in the Signal Iduna Park was also a different feeling, and I am really looking forward to getting to play there again this weekend. It was an amazing feeling for me.”

After four years and just seven appearances, Campbell left Dortmund in search of minutes. He joined Hoffenheim on loan last January, but injuries limited him to only five appearances. He was an unused substitute when Hoffenheim took on Dortmund in April.

That is unlikely to be the case this season. With the exception of the Augsburg match, which he missed because of an injury, Campbell has played every match this season for Elversberg. Even if he doesn't start, it's still likely he comes off the bench for a reunion with Niko Kovač's Borussia Dortmund and Signal Iduna Park.

“It’s a lot of emotions, and it will be very weird to be there and to not be in a Dortmund jersey,” said Campbell. "I am really looking forward to it, and I am very excited to see my friends and old teammates. I think it will be a special moment for me.”

Campbell debuted for the United States national team in October, coming off the bench in a 1-0 win over Canada.

The winger was also eligible for Iceland through his mother's side, initially playing there at youth level. While he's committed to the United States, Campbell takes the influence of both countries with him.

“It’s a mix of both,” said Campbell in an interview with the DFL. "I would say I take a little bit of both, but I feel more at home in the US for sure.”

Campbell was born in Houston, Texas, but his mother was part of the Iceland national team. He moved to Iceland at a young age, and when he was 15, Campbell was playing in Iceland's top flight. He stayed in the country for two years before leaving for Borussia Dortmund.

“I would say I feel more American, but I also like certain parts of Iceland, and a lot of my friends are from there,” said Campbell. “My mom, my grandma, and lots of my family are from there, so I love to go back there to visit."

#2858. Giannis is playing defense like a toddler chasing a ball

It wasn't long ago that Giannis Antetokounmpo was one of the NBA's best defenders. He joined Michael Jordan and Hakeem Olajuwon as the third player ever to be named NBA MVP and Defensive Player of the Year in the same season during the 2019-2020 campaign, and he was consistently a major part of some great units in Milwaukee. Antetokounmpo was always at his best as a 'roamer' who could run around and make plays next to Brook Lopez's reliable rim protection in drop coverage.

Giannis is still roaming after his offseason trade to the Miami Heat, but he doesn't look like the same defender he once was now that he's on the brink of turning 32 years old. Antetokounmpo ranks outside of the top-100 in Dean Oliver's Net-Points Defense stat, and he put some ugly flashes on tape Thursday night as the Golden State Warriors beat the Heat, 120-100.

Antetokounmpo went viral on Thursday for an ugly clip of chasing the ball defensively with absolutely zero purpose. Giannis looked like a big golden retriever out there following the ball wherever it went without actually positioning himself to help make a defensive stop. Watch the clip here:

Giannis looks tired as hell in this clip, and that's understandable. He's the only real offensive creator on the Heat right now, and he's not working with the type of spacing he enjoyed during his heyday with the Bucks. He's putting up a 32.8% usage rate right now, and it's probably too much to ask to carry that level of offensive burden while also being a great defender.

Sharp observers have noticed Giannis' defense starting to decline the last couple seasons. The Heat's best pathway to success this season was being an elite defensive team, and I'm just not sure if they can get there. Miami fell to 3-6 after the loss to the Warriors, and they're lucky to even be that good, because they needed an overtime buzzer-beater to defeat a terrible Los Angeles Clippers team in their previous game.

There's a lot of basketball left to be played, but the Giannis trade feels like a lose-lose for Milwaukee and Miami so far.

#2855. Guardians’ Emmanuel Clase Trial Gets Honest Answers From Bo Naylor

CLEVELAND, OHIO - JUNE 08: Bo Naylor #23 and Emmanuel Clase #48 of the Cleveland Guardians celebrate the team's 4-2 win over the Houston Astros at Progressive Field on June 08, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images)

Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz are on trial in Brooklyn for an alleged pitch rigging scheme from their time pitching with the Cleveland Guardians.

On Thursday, former Guardians catcher Bo Naylor appeared as a defense witness (ahead of schedule so he could fly to Italy to get married this weekend).

Two other catchers are on the witness list — Austin Hedges and Mike Zunino — and will potentially give their testimony later in the trial.

But first it was Naylor who gave his witness to what he knew about what had occurred.

It's certainly a notable perspective on the case to hear from a catcher who was behind the plate when Clase allegedly committed the pitch rigging.

GettyCLEVELAND, OHIO – JUNE 08: Bo Naylor #23 and Emmanuel Clase #48 of the Cleveland Guardians celebrate the team's 4-2 win over the Houston Astros at Progressive Field on June 08, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images)

The Athletic's Sam Blum is covering this trial and provided great details on what was said during Thursday's testimony.

Here's a portion of what he wrote about Naylor:

After watching a video of the allegedly rigged pitch that he caught, Naylor testified it appeared he called the pitch — an outside slider to St. Louis Cardinals hitter Pedro Pagés — using PitchCom. Naylor had already testified that Pages' scouting report suggested low-and-away sliders were Pages' most prominent weakness as a hitter.

"Seems like a pretty good pitch to have as a weapon if you want to induce chase," Naylor testified in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York in Brooklyn.

Blum goes on to write that the defense attorney for Clase pointed out that five of the seven at bats Naylor was catching in which an allegedly rigged pitch occurred still resulted in outs.

Blum writes: "That questioning appeared to be part of a larger strategy to show that throwing pitches off the plate, even intentionally, can still be in furtherance of trying to get the hitter out."

And then Blum added this about the prosecution's questioning of Naylor:

On cross-examination by the government, Naylor was shown video of Clase appearing to shake off signals on two allegedly rigged pitches, implying that Clase was making a conscious decision to throw pitches slower and for a ball, which would lead to payouts on the bets.

The prosecution asked Naylor about Clase's elite command of pitches, but Naylor said Clase was better able to command location on his cut fastball than on his slider.

Once Naylor was done, the trial went back to the prosecution's case, since Naylor had simply gone out of order ahead of his international flight.

The prosecution will have to continue its case before the defense gets to call its other witnesses.

There will eventually be a verdict, and no matter what happens, it's a hugely important case for the future of Major League Baseball and sports betting.

#2854. What makes this 76ers team stacked with superstars so unique

What makes this 76ers team stacked with superstars so unique originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

They're a team of superstars that don't play superstar basketball.

That's the beauty of this 76ers team. They play a brand of unselfish team-first basketball you rarely see from a team loaded with stars.

LeBron James is one of the two or three greatest players in NBA history, a four-time MVP, a four-time NBA champion, a 1st-ballot Hall of Famer.

Joel Embiid is a seven-time all-star, a former MVP, an Olympic gold medalist and a likely Hall of Famer.

Jaylen Brown is a five-time all-star, an NBA champion, a career 20 points-per-game scorer.

Tyrese Maxey is a two-time all-star, one of only two NBA guards averaging 27.0 points per game over the last four years.

Four certified megastars on one team. And somehow they've figured out how to leave their egos at the front door and play smart, tough, disciplined team basketball, the style of ball you just never see on these superstar-laden teams.

On offense, they patiently work the ball around, always looking for the open man or a positive matchup. You've got this bunch of big-name, high-priced All-Stars who are just as happy to pass the ball as shoot it. That never happens.

The 76ers are sixth in the NBA in assists, and they're one of only four teams with twice as many assists as turnovers. Smart, unselfish, patient, disciplined.

When an all-timer like LeBron averages 7.3 assists per game that speaks volumes. LeBron is fifth in the NBA in assists per game among forwards, which is wild. You can see the joy on his face when one of his passes leads to a basket. When one of the greatest players in history has that mentality, it rubs off on everyone around him.

Embiid hasn't really got going yet on offense and still takes too many 3's, but he's also embraced the team-first mentality, and his 4.8 assists per game are more than one full assist above his career average and 4th-most in the NBA among centers or forward-centers. And still one of the most dominating defensive players in the league.

Brown is averaging 27.0 points, which you expect, but he's also averaging 4.3 assists per game, significantly above his career average of 3.8 coming into the season. He's fit in so well so fast you forget its his first season here.

And what can you even say about Maxey? Just a beast. He's averaging nearly 30 points per game but never wastes a possession, always makes the right decision with the ball in his hands and is still finding time to average 4.3 assists per game.

With James, Embiid, Brown and Maxey, the 76ers are the only NBA team with four guys averaging at least 16 points and 4 assists per game. Only the Pacers, Magic and Raptors have three.

But where we're really seeing this group playing out of their minds is on the defensive end, where this bunch of all-stars, including two newcomers, has been astounding.

The 76ers have the 2nd-best defensive efficiency rating in the league, behind only the Pistons, who they play Wednesday night, and they're allowing the 2nd-fewest points in the league, also behind Detroit. Last year, they allowed 123 points per game through eight games. This year they're at 111.

They're holding teams to 43 percent shooting from the field, 3rd-best in the league and their lowest since 2011-12. Their 9.3 steals per game are 6th-most.

All five starters are among the top 25 players in the league in defensive rating – James is fourth, Embiid 11th, Edgecombe 15th, Maxey 22nd and Brown 23rd. How is that even possible?

It's rare to see superstar-caliber guys play as hard on the defensive end as the offensive end. Everybody on this team embraces it. They hustle, they work, they communicate and most importantly they commit to it.

The biggest concern when the 76ers built this dream team was that it would be a team of individuals out for themselves, but the reality has been the opposite.

In a very short period of time, they've learned how to play together. How to play for each other.

And we haven't even mentioned V.J. Edgecomb, who at 21 years old has figured out how to assimilate into this loaded lineup, never force anything, wait for his opportunities and make huge shots when he gets his turn. Edgecombe is at 12.7 points and 3.0 assists per game, and his numbers are understandably down a bit from last year, but if that bothers him it sure doesn't show.

And the role players – Dean Wade, Anfernee Simons, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Jabari Walker – have each adopted the same ego-free style of basketball, supporting the starters however they need to.

Nick Nurse deserves a ton of credit for getting this bunch to play this brand of hoops. It's not easy to get any NBA player to put team goals ahead of individual goals. But he's got Hall of Famers and all-stars doing it and having a blast along the way. They all seem to love playing basketball the right way and they seem to love playing together.

The 76ers are 7-1 and looking like a real threat to win the East, and they're doing it by playing the game the right way.

By committing to each other and not themselves.

#2850. Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double

Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season.

Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists.

On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards.

The Sixers' absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team's matchup with the Pistons on Sunday.

Here are observations on the Sixers' victory Saturday:

Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James' place. He'd missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain.

The 3-and-D forward scored the night's first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession.

Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team's offense in the early going.

The Sixers' seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man.

Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead.

One of Embiid's assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter.

The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn't enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter.

Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run.

Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn't carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly.

Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins' three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead.

The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they'd fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win.

The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team's transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game's first 19 fast-break points.

The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup.

Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup.

Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. None of Brown, Embiid or Maxey had the sort of off night that would have improved the Bucks' odds of a road win. They'd all passed the 20-point mark by the end of the third quarter.

Maxey notched another final-possession bucket, this time with a more conventional make. He canned a jumper from the right elbow with 1.7 seconds left in the third to extend the Sixers' lead to 97-87.

The Bucks made a late push in the fourth quarter. Kel'el Ware's put-back, and-one layup cut the Milwaukee's deficit to 117-114.

The Sixers ultimately handled business. Embiid reached his triple-double by assisting a second-chance Brown jumper and and Caldwell-Pope soon drilled a dagger corner three. Embiid even threw down a last-minute dunk for good measure.

For the second consecutive season, the Sixers have a 3-0 start. They got to four wins last year before dropping their first game.

#2848. Panthers Injury Report & Transactions – Week 9

The Carolina Panthers front office is busy throughout the season with transactions, roster moves, and injury updates. Here's what's happening at Mint Street this week.

Carolina's injury report is scarier than many of last week's Halloween costumes.

Veteran offensive lineman Brady Christensen has been progressing and looks like he will be active this week. He is officially listed as questionable. Provided he's healthy, it will be up to the coaching staff to determine if — and which position — he ends up playing this week. The Panthers offensive line is a shambles right now and Christensen has the versatility to play all five positions. Here's to hoping he's both healthy and productive against the Broncos.

Defensive tackle Bobby Brown is also trending in the right direction after missing last week's game with a hand injury. He was a full participant in practice this week and doesn't have an injury designation as of Friday's practice.

Now, the bad part. Three important contributors to the Panthers defense are in bad shape including outside linebacker Jaelen Phillips, cornerback Will Lee, and linebacker Bobby Okereke. They are all listed as out this week.

On the offensive side of the ball, guard Damien Lewis missed last week's game with a knee injury and is also out against the Broncos.

Signed CB Jakorian Bennett to the practice squad

Jakorian Bennett could help provide reinforcements to the Panthers' bruised and bloodied cornerbacks room. He was originally a 2023 fourth-round pick by the Las Vegas Raiders. In two seasons in Sin City he appeared in 24 games with 11 starts, registering 58 tackles and an impressive 11 passes defended.

After two solid seasons Raiders traded him before the 2025 season to the Philadelphia Eagles. He appeared in 11 games for Philly last year with seven tackles before suffering an injury and getting waived just a few days ago with an injury designation.

Signed OT Da'metrius Weatherspoon to the practice squad

Speaking of battered and bruised units on the Panthers roster, the entire offensive line needs some reinforcement. This week the Panthers signed tackle Da'metrius Weatherspoon to the practice squad. He entered the league this year as an undrafted free agent out of Syracuse and has spent some time with the Bills and Patriots before coming to Charlotte. He has yet to appear in an NFL game.

Signed LB Mohamoud Diabate to the practice squad

If the name Mouhamoud Diabate sounds familiar it's because he's had a decent NFL career in what is now his fifth season. He spent his first three seasons with the Cleveland Browns from 2023 through 2025 appearing in 46 games with 127 tackles. He had a career-high 70 tackles back in 2024.

But his previously promising young career hit a detour last year when he joined the Tennessee Titans and appeared in only one game while bouncing around the practice squad. He now joins the Panthers practice squad with a decent amount of on-field experience.

Releases: This week the Panthers also released CB Zion Childress LB Maema Njongmeta from the practice squad.

#2847. Sixers-Cavs by the numbers: Pressure, threes and a 29-point rematch

Sixers-Cavs by the numbers: Pressure, threes and a 29-point rematch originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers and Cavaliers have already played one game that looked like two.

Cleveland led by 29 points during the Sixers' home opener on Oct. 22 and carried a 69-45 advantage into halftime. Philadelphia responded by winning the second half, 69-37, and completing a 114-106 comeback.

It was the Sixers' largest comeback since the NBA began maintaining detailed play-by-play data in 1997-98. Only nine other teams during that span had overcome a deficit of at least 29 points.

Fifteen days later, the teams will meet again Friday night at Rocket Arena. This time, the matchup counts toward the NBA Cup standings.

The 8-1 Sixers have won five consecutive games and opened group play with a 98-93 victory over the Knicks. The 4-4 Cavs have dropped two straight and will make their Cup debut.

Here are five numbers that help frame the rematch.

Philadelphia's comeback required more than a hot shooting stretch.

The Sixers committed 15 turnovers in the first half, allowing Cleveland to build a 22-6 advantage in points off turnovers. Their pressure then changed the game after halftime.

The Cavs committed 21 turnovers by the end of the night. What had been a 16-point Cleveland advantage in points off turnovers finished even at 22 apiece.

"They upped their pressure and physicality," Cavs head coach Kenny Atkinson said after the game. "It was pretty clear. We did not handle it well."

The Sixers scored 64 of their 69 second-half points through their starting lineup. Tyrese Maxey finished with 28 points, and Philadelphia turned a game that appeared finished into a franchise-record comeback.

The first half of the opening meeting now looks like an exception.

The Sixers have committed 12.9 turnovers per 100 possessions this season, the NBA's second-lowest rate. They are also third in turnover differential, averaging 3.4 fewer giveaways than their opponents.

That is notable for a team that entered the season intending to play faster. Philadelphia has pushed the ball without routinely surrendering possessions.

LeBron James' presence as the primary facilitator has helped. So has Maxey's willingness to move the ball when defenses trap him. Joel Embiid has averaged 5.2 assists, third among qualified centers, and the Sixers have increasingly trusted VJ Edgecombe to make decisions late in games.

Cleveland's defense has not forced many mistakes. The Cavs enter Friday near the bottom of the league in opponent turnover rate.

The first meeting swung when the Sixers stopped giving away possessions and forced Cleveland into mistakes of its own.

The Sixers have allowed 105.1 points per 100 possessions, the NBA's second-best defensive rating. Cleveland enters with the league's ninth-ranked offense.

The Cavs are the only top-10 offense the Sixers have faced through their first nine games.

Philadelphia has held opponents to a 50 percent effective field-goal percentage and 31.8 percent shooting from three-point range. Its defensive shot profile has been encouraging, too. Only 46 percent of opposing three-point attempts have been classified as wide open, the fifth-lowest share in the league, and opponents have taken just 22 percent of their threes from the corners.

There is reason for caution. Based on the quality of shots Philadelphia has allowed, only Washington's opponents have underperformed their expected effective field-goal percentage by a wider margin. The Sixers have defended well, but opponents are unlikely to remain this cold indefinitely.

Cleveland, with Donovan Mitchell, James Harden and Evan Mobley, can test whether those numbers hold against high-level individual shot creation.

The Cavs have attempted exactly 42 three-pointers per game and made 37.2 percent of them.

Cleveland went 7 for 29 from beyond the arc in Philadelphia. Mitchell, Harden and De'Andre Hunter combined to shoot 3 for 17. The Cavs scored 60 points in the paint and still reached 106, but their 24.1 percent performance from three prevented them from stopping the Sixers' comeback.

Friday's game could look considerably different if Cleveland generates its normal volume.

The Sixers have controlled the three-point line well so far, but Mitchell is coming off a 27-point performance against Oklahoma City and scored 32 in the first meeting with Philadelphia. Harden added 16 points that night, although his six turnovers became costly as the Sixers increased their pressure.

Philadelphia has been outrebounded by 5.1 per game. The Cavs rank sixth with 47.5 rebounds per contest.

The Sixers have already shown they can survive a major deficit on the glass. They beat Milwaukee by 11 despite getting outrebounded by 22. That is not a formula they will want to test regularly against Cleveland's size.

Mobley had 18 points and eight rebounds in the first meeting. Jarrett Allen added 14 points and seven boards, helping Cleveland win the rebounding battle, 46-44.

Whether Allen plays Friday remains uncertain.

Cleveland listed Allen as questionable because of a right knee injury after he left Wednesday's loss to Oklahoma City in the first quarter. Allen collided knee-to-knee with Thunder forward Chet Holmgren and did not return.

The Cavs also listed Peyton Watson as questionable with right hamstring soreness and Tyrese Proctor as questionable with an ankle injury. Proctor left Wednesday's game during the fourth quarter. Jaylon Tyson is out with a right ankle sprain.

Allen's availability could significantly alter the matchup on the glass. If he sits, Thomas Bryant would likely handle more of the center minutes behind Mobley. If he plays, Cleveland will have the same starting frontcourt that outrebounded the Sixers during the first meeting.

Atkinson has emphasized the possession battle during Cleveland's two-game slide.

"You've got to get more shots than the other team," he said this week. "Rebounding is a big part of it."

That also carries added importance in the NBA Cup, where point differential is the second tiebreaker after head-to-head results.

Philadelphia enters Friday at 1-0 with a plus-five differential in East Group B. Miami is also 1-0 at plus-20, while Cleveland is playing its first group game.

The Sixers already know they can erase 29 points against the Cavs. A cleaner start would be far more useful than proving it twice.

#2845. Commanders vs. Rams injury report: Washington missing two key receivers

The Commanders receiver corps is being thinned out by injury. Washington will play Sunday's game against the L.A. Rams without Treylon Burks or Dyami Brown, the team announced Friday evening on its official injury report.

Burks is dealing with a foot injury that kept him out of practice all week. Brown suffered a calf injury in Thursday's practice that the Commanders are concerned about.

All this comes shortly after Terry McLaurin was lost for the year with a torn petellar tendon in his knee.

As The Athletic's Nicki Jhabvala originally pointed, Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams were the only receivers at practice who have caught a pass in a game to this point. That's, well, not great.

The injury report was relatively clean outside of that, though the team has absorbed significant recent losses of those — like Javon Kinlaw and Jeremy McNichols — who are now on injured reserve.

Johnny Newton was considered questionable on the injury report, as those on IR with open practice windows usually are. We should learn about his availability on Saturday.

Also, NFL Network reports that superstar Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett is expected to be activated off injured reserve for Sunday's game.

Here's the full Commanders injury report:

WR Dyami Brown – Suffered calf injury during Thursday's practice

WR Treylon Burks – Suffered foot injury vs 49ers

DT Jer'Zhan Newton – 21-day practice window opened; returning from IR (pec)

TE John Bates – Limited all week with a shoulder injury

DL Shy Tuttle – Has a shoulder issue from Week 8

G Sam Cosmi – Dealing with a new knee injury, full practice Friday

OT Josh Conerly – Dealing with a new finger issue

QB Jayden Daniels – Still listed with Week 2 elbow dislocation

#2844. 2. Bundesliga preview: Dynamo Dresden vs. Greuther Fürth

Dynamo Dresden will be looking to end their recent league struggles when they welcome Greuther Fürth on Friday evening, with Thomas Stamm’s side desperate for points as they look to climb away from the bottom of the 2. Bundesliga table.

The hosts head into the Matchday 11 encounter following a disappointing 2-1 defeat against Hannover 96 last weekend. Despite taking the lead through Nicolai Rapp, Dresden were unable to hold onto their advantage, with a second-half comeback leaving them bottom of the table on eight points.

Greuther Fürth, meanwhile, arrive in Saxony with renewed confidence after securing a narrow 1-0 victory over Holstein Kiel. Aaron Keller’s 87th-minute winner secured their third league victory of the campaign, moving Heiko Vogel’s side into ninth place with 12 points.

With just four points separating the two sides, Friday’s encounter presents an important opportunity for both teams to build some momentum heading into the next international break.

Dynamo Dresden have endured an inconsistent return to the second tier since promotion a few years ago and this season is no different, with two victories, two draws and six defeats from their opening ten league fixtures leaving them rooted to the foot of the table.

Stamm’s side have struggled particularly with defensive consistency, conceding 20 goals so far this season while finding the net on 12 occasions.

However, there have been encouraging signs in front of their home supporters. Dresden secured an impressive 2-0 derby victory over 1. FC Magdeburg before following that result with another 2-0 win against Schalke 04 in the DFB-Pokal.

Those performances will offer encouragement ahead of Friday’s encounter, particularly given Fürth’s own struggles for consistency this season.

The defeat against Hannover was nevertheless another frustrating setback. Dresden had looked capable of taking something from the encounter before Friedrich Müller’s dismissal allowed the hosts to take control, with the defender now unavailable for the visit of Fürth.

Stamm will therefore be demanding a response from his players, particularly in their defensive organisation and ability to maintain their intensity throughout the full 90 minutes.

Speaking ahead of the game, the Dynamo head coach acknowledged the quality of the opposition but insisted his side should approach the encounter with confidence.

“I expect a team that plays bravely with the ball and intensely against it. They resolve difficult situations with purpose. We need a really good performance, but we don’t need to hide at home.”

Stamm also stressed the importance of remaining positive, urging his players not to become frustrated if their early opportunities fail to find the back of the net.

Greuther Fürth travel to Dresden looking to build on their recent victory over Holstein Kiel, which ended a frustrating run of results and provided a welcome boost for Vogel’s side.

The visitors have collected 12 points from their opening ten league fixtures, recording three victories, three draws and four defeats. Their 13 goals scored suggest they possess some attacking quality, although 16 goals conceded highlight an area that still requires improvement.

Fürth’s biggest challenge this season has arguably been finding consistency. Their victory over Eintracht Braunschweig was followed by a disappointing 3-0 defeat against Osnabrück, before they returned to winning ways against Kiel.

The late nature of their most recent victory should nevertheless provide some confidence, with Aaron Keller finding the net in the 87th minute to secure all three points.

Vogel will be hoping his side can now register consecutive league victories for the first time this season, although he is well aware of the difficulties associated with travelling to Dresden.

The Fürth head coach has called for a better balance between defensive organisation and attacking intent, particularly after his side struggled to create opportunities in recent outings.

“Good positioning in attack is always the foundation for creating scoring opportunities. We need to be more precise in that area than we have been in recent matches.” Vogel explained ahead of the encounter.

The visitors will also be keen to avoid a repeat of their previous trip to Dresden, when they suffered a 2-0 defeat in January.

With experienced attacking players such as the league’s joint top-scorer Felix Klaus alongside the creativity of Ole Pohlmann, Fürth will certainly possess the tools to trouble their hosts if they can find the right balance going forward.

Friday’s encounter will be the 19th competitive meeting between the two sides, with Greuther Fürth holding the historical advantage.

The visitors have recorded nine victories compared to Dynamo Dresden’s four, while the remaining five encounters have ended in draws.

However, Dresden will take encouragement from their most recent meeting, which took place at the Rudolf-Harbig-Stadion in January 2026.

Goals from Thomas Keller and Jakob Lemmer secured a convincing 2-0 victory for the hosts, marking the beginning of an important run of results in their battle to secure survival last season.

Interestingly, that victory was Fürth’s only defeat in their previous nine meetings with Dresden, with the Franken side recording five victories and three draws during that period.

Vogel’s men will therefore be hoping to reassert their historical dominance, while Dresden will be looking to repeat their January performance and secure another important home victory.

Dynamo Dresden have several important absentees to contend with ahead of Friday’s fixture, particularly in the defensive department.

Friedrich Müller is suspended following his red card against Hannover, while Brooklyn Ezeh is also unavailable due to suspension following his dismissal for the club’s Under-21 side.

Lars Bünning and Kenneth Schmidt remain sidelined with longer-term injuries, while Thomas Keller continues to be unavailable following his concussion.

Luca Herrmann has also joined the injury list after picking up an injury against Hannover.

For Greuther Fürth, Maxim Dal remains sidelined through injury, although Vogel should otherwise have a relatively settled squad available.

Dynamo Dresden (4-2-3-1): Grill; Sterner, Muhamedbegovic, Rapp, Rossipal; Wagner, Raschl; Bobzien, Hauptmann, Čović; Vermeij

Greuther Fürth (4-2-3-1): Hellstern; Dehm, Heuer, Blank, Itter; Will, Bansé; Klaus, Pohlmann, Keller; Sillah

#2843. Bona doubtful, no Sixers starters on injury report for Cavs game

Bona doubtful, no Sixers starters on injury report for Cavs game originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers listed backup center Adem Bona as doubtful for their Friday night meeting with the Cavaliers.

Bona's official listing on the team's Thursday evening injury report was "cervical spine sprain."

He played one of his better games so far this season Wednesday in the 8-1 Sixers' win over the Pistons, slamming in two second-quarter dunks and posting five points, two rebounds, a steal and an assist in 15 minutes.

Bona headed back to the Sixers' locker room with 8:56 left in the fourth quarter. Sixers head coach Nick Nurse told reporters postgame that the 23-year-old big man had "neck soreness" after taking a hit.

Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear) will remain out for the Sixers in Cleveland. The Sixers beat the 4-4 Cavs in dramatic fashion on Oct. 22, overcoming a 29-point deficit to win a wild home opener. If Bona were to miss Friday's game, Jabari Walker would be the logical next name in line at center behind Joel Embiid.

Notably, the Sixers included no starters on their injury report.

Tyrese Maxey had an apparent late-game injury concern Wednesday night when he seemed to hurt his right hand on an intentional Detroit foul.

However, Maxey told reporters postgame he would "be fine" and it looks like he'll be good to go against the Cavs.
