#2842. Florida high school football’s new Open Division is loaded: Meet the 8-team field

The Florida High School Athletic Association is introducing a new postseason format in 2026, bringing eight of the state's top high school football programs together to compete for the inaugural Open Division championship.

The field features an intriguing mix of nationally ranked contenders, traditional state powers and programs looking to prove they belong among Florida's best. Spoiler: There are a ton of heavy hitters.

Here's a look at the eight teams that made the inaugural FHSAA Open Division playoff bracket:

As expected, St. Thomas Aquinas enters the inaugural Open Division as Florida's top-ranked program. The Raiders finished the regular season undefeated at 10-0 and holds the No. 2 spot in the latest USA TODAY Super 25 rankings and the top spot in the USA TODAY Southeast Super 15. Having already beaten Columbus and Chaminade-Madonna this season, Roger Harriott's group enters the gauntlet trying to finish 15-0 but will be without Notre Dame commit Julius Jones Jr. after season-ending surgery earlier this year. Expect the defense and the run game to try and win games for the Raiders.

The Explorers have been outstanding this season under Dave Dunn, finishing out with a 9-1 record with the lone loss coming to St. Thomas Aquinas in Week 3. Columbus currently sits at No. 5 in the USA TODAY Super 25, and second in the USA TODAY Super 15 Southeast region. The Explorers stunned then-No. 1 nationally ranked Bishop Gorman (NV) 33-28 in August, announcing themselves as a legitimate national contender. Expect 5-star ATH A'mir Sears and QB Kai Moore to make their presences felt in these games.

The Bulls are off back-to-back state titles and enter the postseason with a 9-1 record. West Boca went unbeaten against in-state competition, having only lost to St. John's (DC) by one point in a 15-14 loss. The defense of Dylan Potts' squad has been elite this year, allowing just 46 points over 10 games. Expect this unit to be tested against some high-octane offenses, but the offensive unit led by QB Trey Moran, WR Billy Clancy III, and others can score points too.

The Lions have put together one heck of a season built by transfers, going 8-2 with losses to top-seeded St. Thomas Aquinas and Sierra Canyon (CA) as part of the Broward Showcase. The Lions are 13th in the USA TODAY Super 15 Southeast rankings, fueled by QB Brady Quinn and a wide receiver corps of Tromon Isaac, Kedarius Rhaney, and Armani Strong along with RB Amos Bradford. The Lions defeated American Heritage 46-27 and closed their regular season with four consecutive victories.

Lakeland has put together an outstanding season, finishing 9-1 with a double-overtime loss to Venice in Week 2. The Dreadnaughts have leaned on the versatility of senior Kelin Hendrix, who has contributed as both a passer and runner, throwing 17 touchdown passes while adding 10 rushing touchdowns. Senior running back Xavion Mitchell has provided another dimension to the offense, leading the team with 638 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns. Lakeland closed its regular season with a 35-0 shutout of The First Academy, effectively eliminating the Lions from Open Division contention.

Miami Central has perhaps the most challenging résumé of any team entering the Open Division with three regular season losses but enter as the No. 6 seed in the Open Division. The Rockets opened their schedule with a 23-22 road victory over Orange Lutheran (CA) before traveling north to face Buford (GA), falling 18-7. They also suffered a 28-3 loss to fellow Open Division qualifier Columbus and closed the regular season with a 27-10 defeat against Carol City. Those results tell part of the story, but Central also demonstrated its offensive ceiling with a 52-10 victory over Northwestern and a 63-7 win against Key West.

Raines might be bringing the most momentum of any team in the inaugural field. The Vikings finished 10-0, extending their overall winning streak to 24 games and completing their third consecutive undefeated regular season. Their calling card has been a defense capable of changing games in a hurry, allowing just 10.7 points per game with 19 takeaways this year. Quarterback Samon Ellison-Morgan and running back TJ Williamson provide the offensive production, while defensive lineman Chenaniah Doran and edge rusher Troy Butler have been disruptive up front.

Venice has a legitimate offensive centerpiece in senior running back Dorien Irving-Jones, who has been one of the most productive backs in Southwest Florida this season. Irving-Jones averaged 148.6 rushing yards per game and accounted for 24 total touchdowns, giving the Indians a reliable offensive identity built around their ground attack. Senior Ira Dale has provided another rushing option, while freshman receiver and return specialist Mike Blakley has emerged as an intriguing playmaker with 63.3 receiving yards per game and six receiving touchdowns.

Just missed: Carrollwood Day (Tampa, FL), Cardinal Newman (West Palm Beach, FL), American Heritage (Plantation, FL)

Follow Sports Reporter Alex Martin on X at @AlexMartinUSAT or via email: amartin@usatodayco.com. For additional high school sports coverage, be sure to follow USA TODAY High School Sports on Instagram and X.

#2841. Lions, Dolphins Week 9 injury designations: Lions rule out 5 starters

The Detroit Lions (5-2) and Miami Dolphins (1-6) have declared their Week 9 injury designations, and the Lions will be missing multiple starters, including one on offense, three on defense, and one not yet cleared from his injury list—all of which we knew ahead of time, based on coach Dan Campbell's comments throughout the week.

Let's look at Friday's practice report and get you up to date on what we know.

Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded.

C Cade Mays (ankle) — Preparing for Juice Scruggs to start

S Kerby Joseph (knee, PUP) — Days remaining in injury evaluation clock: 11

Mays is dealing with a low ankle sprain, which typically keeps players out at least a week, and potentially as long as a month, so him being ruled out of this game was expected. How quickly he recovers is still to be determined, but the Lions have been highly fortunate to have Juice Scruggs stepping into the starting center role, and they've been planning on him starting since the beginning of this week.

Wonnum is still working through the NFL's concussion protocols and won't be able to return in time for this game. With head injury recovery times varying by individual, it's unclear how long he will need before he is cleared. Second-round rookie Derrick Moore is expected to increase his role in Wonnum's absence, and Campbell is seeing improvement:

"It was unfortunate we lost Wonnum, but yet, now (Moore) gets more reps. And the reps that he got are valuable, man. There's no way to duplicate real in time game reps against good opponents and you see growth, you see growth. I saw growth in practice yesterday. So, the more he plays, the better he's going to get. And we love where he's going right now."

Jack Campbell continues to improve, per Dan Campbell, but he should be considered out indefinitely until otherwise clarified.

"Jack continues to improve, which is all great news," Dan Campbell said on Friday.

Reed said he felt good in the locker room following the game, but he was not cleared to practice this week and will miss this game. Campbell noted that he's very confident with the team's depth:

"(Ennis) Rakestraw is getting better. Rock (Ya-Sin) looks healthy and is playing good football. (Roger) McCreary, too. So, I just feel like these guys are starting to play pretty good football for us. And (Khalil) Dorsey, man, Dorsey's contributing in a big way. So, I like where we're at and it's really a pretty depthwise, it's a pretty strong room. So yeah, I don't like the though of not having Reed, but at the same time, I'm encouraged. I'm encouraged. I think we'll be OK here."

Joseph is looking "better than anticipated," according to safeties coach Jim O'Neil, but Campbell made it clear earlier in the week that the plan was to keep him out for another game, then continue to ramp up his participation levels next week, as he nears a return.

"It's been great. Two weeks ago, it was classroom work, where we were really locked in. Then it was walkthrough and individual. Yesterday was his first team practice and he looked a lot better than what I anticipated him looking (like). So it was very encouraging. So now he's gotta stack multiple days. He's got to stack them, so today will be a big day for him, but he looked awesome yesterday at practice," O'Neill said on Friday.

RB Sione Vaki (ankle) — added to the injury report on Friday

Vaki was unexpectedly absent from Friday's practice and has been given a questionable designation heading into this weekend's game. Beyond that, the extent of his injury is unknown, and we may have to wait until Saturday—to see if he travels with the team—or even game time on Sunday, to find out his availability.

Saylors has dealt with a neck injury for two weeks and couldn't finish Week 7's game against the Vikings because of it. Look for the Lions to be cautious in his return, but with Vaki also questionable, the Lions could end up with a depth issue at running back.

St. Brown was injured in Week 7 but told the media on Thursday that, "I'm a little banged up, but I'll be alright," and is anticipating playing against the Dolphins.

Ogbongbemiga was estimated to have been a limited participant on Wednesday and a full participant after that, and with him not carrying an injury designation, he should be good to go, giving the Lions special teams work and linebacker depth.

Ya-Sin dealt with cramps earlier in the week but still practiced in full each day. He's potentially in line to challenge for a starting role this week with Reed sidelined.

Branch is nearing the end of the NFL's concussion protocol, and Campbell said he expects him to be cleared and ready to play on Sunday.

"I think (Brian Branch) BB's going to be good here. We'll get through today, and I think we'll be OK."

#2840. Observations after Sixers beat Bulls to reach East-leading 7-1

Observations after Sixers beat Bulls to reach East-leading 7-1 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers kept up their hot start to the season Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, reaching 7-1 with a 126-107 win against the Bulls.

All five of the Sixers' starters scored in double figures. Tyrese Maxey posted 26 points on 10-for-15 shooting and 11 assists. Jaylen Brown tallied a season-best 25 points and 11 rebounds.

VJ Edgecombe's 21 points were a new season high. LeBron James recorded 15 points, nine assists and seven boards.

Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson had 24 points and seven rebounds.

Joel Embiid (15 points, eight rebounds) had been listed as questionable with an official designation of "right foot plantar fascia injury management." He sat out Saturday on the second night of a back-to-back for the Sixers' win over the Hornets.

"Plantar is a little bit of a come and go type of thing," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse told reporters pregame. "They're just trying to manage it. It's very painful, if you've ever had it. It can kind of come and go out of nowhere. So we're just trying to manage the pain with that, be as smart as we can."

Nurse told reporters that Dominick Barlow is set to see a specialist Tuesday about the back injury that's sidelined him to start the season.

"He's been on court a little bit … not a ton of moving around," Nurse said. "I think they want to get to tomorrow's appointment. Hopefully, it'll be positive and we can get into his workouts a little bit."

The Sixers will begin a three-game road trip Wednesday when they visit the Pistons. Here are observations on their victory Monday:

After Embiid blitzed a Bulls pick-and-roll, Maxey picked off Matas Buzelis' hurried pass to get the Sixers rolling in transition and James jammed home the team's first field goal.

Edgecombe got a slam soon after James grabbed a defensive rebound and the Sixers again pushed the pace. The Sixers scored six quick fast-break points, leading the Bulls to burn an early timeout, and James' long-distance feeds were a major asset.

"If you're open, he's going to pass it," Edgecombe said of James. "The main thing is just being ready. Tonight I had to run and go get 'em. If you're open and he sees you, he's going to pass the ball."

Edgecombe had a dunk-heavy first quarter. He threw down his second when Dean Wade nabbed a steal and dropped off a typically selfless dish to the Sixers' explosive second-year guard, whose slam put the team up 22-13.

The Sixers have an abundance of dangerous options in the open floor, Edgecombe included. As he's already shown with his continued clutch shotmaking, the 21-year-old won't become anything resembling a non-factor offensively this year as a byproduct of the Sixers' enhanced star power.

Over the team's first seven games, Edgecombe had averaged 11.3 points. He scored 11 in the first period on 5-for-5 shooting.

Adem Bona missed a dunk early in the second quarter, which stung a bit more when Jalen Smith drilled a three-pointer seconds later.

Bona remained the Sixers' main backup center. He had a poor first-half stint overall amid a largely negative start to his third season. The 23-year-old big man played well in the Sixers' victory over the Bucks, posting six points, 13 rebounds and three blocks. Outside of that, his season has been sparse on bright moments so far. It's reasonable to wonder when Nurse might turn to alternatives like Jabari Walker, who played a good game Saturday in Charlotte, or try James again at the five.

The Bulls outscored the Sixers by eight points in Bona's first run, cutting their derficit to 40-38. Chicago went in front with a three by former Sixer Buddy Hield.

The Sixers regained the advantage late in the second quarter. Maxey and James each were excellent as passers in the first half, combining for 14 assists and three turnovers. James fired the ball to Wade for a corner three that gave the Sixers a 60-52 lead.

Following a third-quarter Embiid fadeaway jumper and two James lay-ins, the Sixers were up 17 points.

The Bulls cut the Sixers' lead down to 11 points by the start of the fourth quarter. With Bona still struggling and on four fouls, Wade began the fourth at center. Bona then briefly spelled Wade before being whistled for his fifth foul and taking a seat. Embiid ultimately wasn't needed for any of the fourth period and only logged 25 minutes.

Embiid said postgame that he was not available to return to the action in the fourth and has been feeling his plantar fasciitis on the court. The seven-time All-Star's health is clearly not close to 100 percent.

"I was on a minutes restriction," he said. "(The foot) has been going like that for the past few weeks. It's painful. Just got to manage it.

"If it flares up pretty bad, got to take a step back. We've been able to manage it, but it has its ups and downs."

The Sixers' lead got as low as eight points, but Chicago did not shoot well enough from three-point range (26.3 percent) or have sufficient firepower to sustain a meaningful comeback run. The bottom line is the Sixers are in a different class than the Bulls, who fell to 1-6.

As for the Sixers, they'll wake up Tuesday morning at the top of the Eastern Conference standings.

"You've got some of these nights where you kind of call them professional wins. …You look at the records and all that kind of stuff, but they have a lot of talent," Nurse said. "A lot of these teams play a way that's a little scary. It's fast and it's furious, lots of threes. … They're going to keep coming at you, high-possession games. So they're not easy games and I'm glad that we handled it professionally tonight."

#2838. Saquon Barkley set to play as Eagles remain without DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks

Eagles running back Saquon Barkley is on track to play against his former team.

Barkley remained limited in practice on Friday with hamstring and back injuries, but he has no injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants. Barkley missed a couple of games with the hamstring injury and has been limited to 32 offensive snaps the last two weeks.

While quarterback Joe Milton will have Barkley with him in the backfield for his first Eagles start, he'll be missing wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Smith and Wicks are both going to miss their third straight game.

#2837. ‘I'm finding my footing': Jaylen Brown's role taking shape with Sixers

'I'm finding my footing': Jaylen Brown's role taking shape with Sixers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Jaylen Brown has spent the opening weeks of the season describing the Sixers as a work in progress.

He offered a similarly humble perspective Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena. His performance, however, provided the clearest look yet at how he can influence this group while sharing the floor with the club's other established stars.

Brown finished with 25 points, 11 rebounds and five assists in the Sixers' 126-107 win over the Chicago Bulls. He shot 9 for 15 from the field, made four three-pointers and did not commit a turnover.

Five of his rebounds came on the offensive end, an area Brown has emphasized while the Sixers continue piecing together their frontcourt rotation.

"Just a mindset," Brown said. "Just trying to create extra opportunities for my team. As we're trying to patch together our fives and our front line, I try to make an extra contribution and emphasis on the glass."

Brown has also been careful about how he describes his place on a roster that already belonged to Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey.

Maxey scored 15 of his 26 points in the fourth quarter Monday, continuing his torrid start to the season. He has led the Sixers in scoring while being the only starter to appear in all eight games.

Brown is not interested in interrupting that.

"Maxey's been leading the way, 100 percent," Brown said. "He's been here. This is his team. Him and Joel have been here for a while, so the mindset has been to complement those guys. I'm finding my footing, but Maxey has been leading the way for sure."

Brown's footing looked firm against Chicago.

Beyond his scoring, he helped the Sixers control the glass, moved the ball within an offense that generated 23 assists during the first half and supplied the physicality Nick Nurse expects from him.

"The dude is tough and he wins," Nurse said. "I'll take that all day long. The degree of difficulty on some of the shots he hit was really amazing. I thought he pounded the glass and got some key rebounds. Makes a lot of winning plays. Man, he's a winner."

Brown spent the first 10 years of his career in Boston. He won a championship there, reached another NBA Finals and grew from a 20-year-old prospect into one of the league's premier two-way wings.

Moving into a new system alongside James, Embiid and Maxey was never going to be seamless.

"I mean, he's fitting in along with all of us," James said. "We're getting better and better. It's not going to happen overnight. He spent his first 10 years in a system in Boston, in the city, so it's going to take some adjustment.

"It takes adjustment for him. It's going to take adjustment for the rest of the guys that joined this franchise as well. But tonight was a great step."

James pointed to Brown's "pressure, his shot-making ability, his rebounding ability" and his professionalism.

Brown's early influence has extended beyond his production.

The Sixers entered Monday with one of the NBA's best half-court defenses. Brown has been one of the group's most persistent voices, stressing communication, preparation and attention to opposing players' tendencies.

"That's the part that I care about the most as a group, not individually," Brown said. "Having a mentality night in and night out, respecting your opponent, respecting the game, making sure that we are executing our coverages, we're being clear in our communication and then we're also taking away tendencies on a night-to-night basis.

"Those things I just explained are over 50 percent of the battle."

Brown understands that maintaining those details across an 82-game schedule will require more than reminders.

"A little bit of accountability," he said. "You learn different guys require different things. How you communicate with each guy may be a little different, but accountability for sure and confrontation if need be.

"The offense is going to be what it's going to be, but our defense has got to be non-negotiable. That's something I say all the time. Non-negotiable. You want to be a good team, defense is non-negotiable."

The Sixers showed both sides of their defensive potential Monday.

They built a double-digit lead during the first half, allowed Chicago to score 36 points in the second quarter and then created separation after halftime. Philadelphia held the Bulls to 20 points in the third quarter before pulling away in the fourth.

Brown did not celebrate their ability to raise their intensity after it slipped.

"I don't like that we have that," he said. "It's good that we have shown the potential, but we've got to keep that switch on. It doesn't work like that where you just flip the switch.

"It can catch up to us and it can bite us against a better team or on a night that we're not being as crisp on offense. It can't be a switch just because we're playing a lesser opponent or whatever the case may be. We've got to make sure that mentality is from the beginning to end. Can't skip any steps."

That urgency accompanies considerable optimism.

Brown said the Sixers enjoy playing together. He loves when James grabs a rebound because "he's like a quarterback," capable of launching an outlet pass or immediately pushing the pace.

The group is learning when to attack, when to move the ball and how to avoid hesitating in its effort to play unselfishly.

"It's a lot of talent, man," Brown said. "We like each other, and we're just kind of building that chemistry of how we can get this thing to a well-oiled machine. I think we're taking steps forward every single day."

The Sixers are 7-1 despite Brown believing those steps remain incomplete. They have won close games, erased sizable deficits and received important contributions from different players.

Brown's performance Monday showed another version of how their pieces can fit.

"We still have a long way to go to being a really, really solid, great team," Brown said. "But we've been able to win some games. We started out the season great, 7-1, and you haven't seen our best version yet.

#2836. NFL analyst praises Cam Heyward for continued dominance at 37 years old

Pittsburgh Steelers defensive tackle Cameron Heyward is one of the oldest active players in the NFL, but you wouldn't guess it from how incredible he's playing in 2026. That isn't lost on well-respected NFL analyst Brian Baldinger, who pointed out how Cameron Heyward continues to defy Father Time.

On a new episode of The Best Football Show podcast, Baldinger explained how blown away he's been with how elite Heyward is playing at 37 years old.

"Cam Heyward, he's in his 16th year, he might never have played better than he is right now," Baldinger said. "He's batting down balls. He's destroying guards. He ran right through the rookie guard [Austin] Barber, the left guard Zion Johnson. He destroyed those guys."

Heyward has been nothing short of dominant through eight games this season, recording 28 combined tackles, three tackles for loss, six batted-down passes, and 2.5 sacks.

Heyward is a major component of Pittsburgh's defensive resurgence in 2026, and it wouldn't be surprising if the veteran defensive tackle is able to add another first-team All-Pro honor to his seemingly Hall of Fame-worthy resume.

#2835. Chicago Bears stadium proposal on Southeast Side gains attention as lawmakers work on legislation

A proposal for a new Chicago Bears stadium on the city's Southeast Side is gaining attention as lawmakers work on stadium legislation ahead of the fall veto session.

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell accompanied Bears officials Kevin Warren and George McCaskey to a meeting with Illinois legislative leaders in Chicago earlier this week.

The discussions come as a new potential stadium location is being promoted at the former U.S. Steel site on the South Side.

Developer Related Midwest has released renderings of a proposed domed Bears stadium at the site. Company President Curt Bailey said the proposal has been presented to both the Bears and lawmakers who will return for the fall veto session later this month.

"It's iconic for the Bears to be in Chicago, to be on the lakefront. You think about those shots of the skyline and the lake and the Chicago Bears," Bailey said.

The stadium concept includes a window at the north end designed to showcase the Chicago skyline.

SEE ALSO | Chicago architecture firm proposes renderings of new Bears stadium near current White Sox location

Bailey said the Southeast Side location has been on the Bears' radar for four to five months. He said the property had previously been slated for a large data center project, but Related Midwest shifted plans as public sentiment toward such developments changed.

"When you talk about the the size of the the site, the ability to do all of the things around the stadium that you want to do, whether it's retail or entertainment, you know this site that we're talking about is 9 miles from Soldier Field," Bailey said.

Bailey noted the site is much closer to Soldier Field than the property the Bears already own in Arlington Heights.

READ MORE | Illinois lawmakers weigh stadium authority plan for Bears Arlington Heights option

In a statement, the Bears said they are continuing to pursue locations in Hammond, Indiana.

"The Chicago Bears remain committed to building a world-class stadium and mixed-use district for our fans, the Chicagoland community and the team. We continue to work collaboratively with local and state leaders in Indiana to advance our stadium development plans in Hammond, where we are finalizing due diligence details across two sites in the Wolf Lake area. At the same time, we appreciate the recent engagement from Illinois leadership to explore legislation which has allowed us to share our feedback. We expect productive dialogue with both leadership teams in the coming weeks. We have a responsibility and obligation to explore every option available to the club, and we look forward to developing a transformational project that will attract global events and deliver jobs and economic growth to all of Chicagoland," the statement said.

Bears officials have promised to continue conversations about a path forward for a stadium in Arlington Heights or Chicago, as well, according to ESPN's Ian Rapoport.

Gov. JB Pritzker said stadium legislation being developed by lawmakers could allow the Bears to pursue the Southeast Side location.

"This is up to the Bears. You know, there's a bill that's being put together that gives the Bears the opportunity to choose where they want to build a stadium in Illinois, and then it's going to be up to them where it goes," Pritzker said.

Pritzker said he wants the legislation to be ready during the first week of the veto session, which begins Nov. 17, so it could be voted on during the second week, which begins Dec. 1.

#2833. Observations after Sixers earn strong road win over Pistons, Brown scores 30

Observations after Sixers earn strong road win over Pistons, Brown scores 30 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers remain the Eastern Conference's sole leader.

They earned a 112-106 road win over the Pistons on Wednesday night to move to 8-1 on the season and stay at the top of the standings. Detroit fell to 6-2.

The Sixers last started 8-1 in the 2023-24 season, which was Nick Nurse's first as the team's head coach.

Jaylen Brown scored a season-high 30 points and pulled down seven rebounds.

Joel Embiid had 26 points and a season-best 15 rebounds. LeBron James posted 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists. Tyrese Maxey added 19 points and seven assists.

The Pistons' leading scorers were Duncan Robinson with 27 points and Cade Cunningham with 26.

The Sixers were down Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The Pistons' injured players included Jalen Duren (right hamstring strain) and Isaiah Joe (right hip contusion).

Nurse told reporters in Detroit he thinks "it'll be another 10 to 12 days before they kind of clear (Barlow) for getting on the court to see where he is," according to Sixers Wire's Ky Carlin.

The Sixers will visit the Cavaliers on Friday night. Here are observations on their victory over Detroit:

Embiid assisted the Sixers' first basket with a sharp pass out of a double team. He saw Brown's cut along the baseline and dished to him for a layup.

Detroit ran several double drag screen actions early, forcing Embiid to defend on the perimeter. The Pistons started 7 for 11 from the floor and took a 17-11 edge on a Robinson three-pointer.

The Sixers then made a 10-0 run and Embiid was right in the middle of it. He converted a put-back layup after a pretty high-low feed from James. Embiid hit two foul shots to give the Sixers the lead. The team raised its defensive level and Detroit's offense grew frigid.

Embiid was very good on the glass in the first half, grabbing eight rebounds. The Sixers had an excellent rebounding game as a team, limiting the Pistons to four offensive boards over 48 minutes.

Embiid didn't break out of his early-season three-point shooting slump, going 0 for 3. He's 3 for 26 (11.5 percent) on the season and hasn't made a three since the Sixers' second game.

Late in the second quarter, Embiid got into a dead-ball dust-up with Tolu Smith. After an officials' review, Embiid was assessed a technical foul for "initiating" the altercation.

Playing on his 26th birthday, Maxey missed his first four field goals and was scoreless until he hit a floater with 31.5 seconds left in the first quarter.

Brown picked up the scoring slack, tallying 10 points in the first on 4-for-6 shooting and hitting a deep, buzzer-beating three to put the Sixers up 29-21. He produced at all three levels, chose smart spots to attack and looked comfortable in the rhythm of the Sixers' offense.

Meanwhile, James did his usuall stellar work as a passer. He assisted two Adem Bona slams in the second quarter and constantly spotted open teammates. Nurse rewarded Bona's strong opening stint, playing him for a lengthy stretch.

Brown swished a corner triple to extend the Sixers' lead to 48-31. With a 3-for-5 night, Brown is at 45.7 percent from long distance so far this season. It wouldn't be surprising at all if Brown's three-point shooting improved from last season's 34.7 percent clip. With such an abundance of star power, the Sixers' hope will be that everyone gets regular open looks beyond the arc throughout the year.

As for Maxey, he sat with 3:26 left in the second quarter after being whistled for his third foul. Even with a mere two points from Maxey, the Sixers entered halftime holding a 14-point advantage.

The Pistons played better basketball to begin the third quarter.

Following a John Collins alley-oop jam, Nurse called timeout with his team's lead down to single digits. The Pistons' offense sustained some success, but the Sixers prevented a sustained run.

Embiid played an especially physical, aggressive third quarter. He tipped in his own miss and Maxey then sunk a three to make the Sixers' lead 84-68. They were up as many as 17 points in the third.

Embiid sat out the fourth quarter Monday night for the Sixers' win over the Bulls and said he was on a minutes restriction (25) because of his right foot plantar fasciitis. He played the fourth period against the Pistons and logged 33 minutes. Bona went back to the locker room early in the fourth. Nurse told reporters postgame that Bona had "neck soreness."

Detroit did not let the Sixers coast to victory.

Robinson drained a three. Cunningham made a pair of free throws and drove in for a layup that cut the Pistons' deficit to 106-102.

The Sixers halted the Pistons' run before anything disastrous was on the table. Brown blocked a Cunningham three-point try, Embiid knocked down two foul shots, and the East's No. 1 early-season team improved to 4-0 on the road.

#2832. LeBron James is having fun in Philly and one fan's wine can prove it

LeBron James is having fun in Philly and one fan's wine can prove it originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

LeBron James is one of kind in so many ways. What he did Monday night might be the cherry on top.

In the third quarter of the Sixers' 126-107 victory over the Bulls, James decided he'd take fan interaction to a whole new level.

James looked for a transition pass from Tyrese Maxey, who snagged a rebound. James was behind the pass and his momentum took him into the stands, where he disappeared for a few moments.

It wasn't until another angle was shown on replay that we could see what actually went down in the darkness of the seats. James didn't hold back giving reporters a play-by-play.

"I spilled some of his wine," he said postgame. "I crashed into him, spilled some of his wine. So I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm and how good it was. It was alright."

Troy Clemons – the Sixers fan whose drink spilled – explained his perspective on the interaction with James to Kris Rhim of ESPN.

"[I was] walking to my seat … LeBron crashed into me, he grabbed me, he said 'My bad,' my drink spilled everywhere. He took my drink from me and he basically just took a sip of it, gave it back and ran back on the [court]."

"At the end of the day he's another man like me," Clemons said. "I mean he's LeBron, but at the end of the day, I threw that cup in the trash. And it's nothing up with him, I just got a fresh drink though."

It should be noted that players are not supposed to drink from fans' cups, but it's rare for the NBA to fine someone for a spontaneous interaction such as this. In 2019, a similar thing happened when Mike Scott tumbled into the Bucks' court-side seats. The Sixers star jokingly took a sip of a fan's beverage and the NBA opted not to fine him. Time will tell if James has the same fate.

If nothing else, an interaction like this just shows how much fun James seems to be having.

The 24-year veteran noted the importance of finding joy in the game as he grinds through the season.

"It's a long marathon. And if you don't find ways to have fun throughout it, even though you're working and even though you're locked in, then it could wear on you. So for me, especially at this point in my career, being able to just appreciate the moments, the small moments, these fans are great to us. We try to be great to them as well. By playing the game the right way, playing the game hard and then also just being showmen as well, it was a great game for us."

Head coach Nick Nurse also weighed in on the 41-year-old's mindset coming into the season.

"This summer I think he probably stated publicly that he wanted to go some place and have some fun playing. He loves the game, [it's his] 24th year. It's a group of guys, like I keep saying, that have been super focused in the intent of playing the right way. I think he's a big part of that."

The vibes are high. It's difficult for them not to be.

With Monday's win against the Bulls, the Sixers are 7-1 and lead the Eastern Conference. They've won four in a row and the only team they've lost to is the Pistons. The Sixers will face them on Wednesday to start a three-game road trip.

#2831. Bold predictions as UC tries to win at No. 17 Houston Nov. 7

The latest Big 12 quarterback the Cincinnati Bearcats must face is a 6-foot-3 gunslinger from Cypress, Texas, about 30 miles from the University of Houston.

Conner Weigman is in his fifth year of football and has thrown for 2,053 yards and 20 touchdowns with just two interceptions this season. He is in his second year with Houston after playing at Texas A&M. He threw for 2,705 yards and 25 touchdowns last season, when the Cougars struggled to a 4-8 mark.

This season, Houston's third-down offensive efficiency is tops in the nation. Weigman also has 249 yards with his legs and six touchdowns.

UC quarterback JC French IV has thrown for 1,773 yards and 13 touchdowns with only three interceptions. A year ago, he threw for more yards than Weigman with 2,929 at Georgia Southern.

UC Bearcats football Overreactions, extended grades from UC Bearcats vs. No. 6 Utah Utes

French is heading toward career-highs on the ground. For UC to be successful against Houston's high-powered offense, they will likely need another successful day running the football and an error-free day in the air.

Defensively, the Bearcats have to keep Houston below their averages of 36 points and 470 total offensive yards.

"I think first down will be critical this week against Houston," UC head coach Scott Satterfield said. "They're so efficient. They don't have many negative plays. If we can try to knock them off a little on first down, it will make that third down a little bit longer. These offenses, when it's third and three or four or less, they can do everything. It makes it a lot more difficult to stop them. If you get them in that long-yardage scenario, you get a better idea of how to get them off the field."

Cole Tabb did have 131 yards vs. Utah, and Gi'Bran Payne had 67. In four of their five wins, UC has had over 250 rushing yards. A healthy Payne should help, as well as anything either can offer in the passing game.

Utah ran for 226 yards against Houston in their most recent game Oct. 24, a 21-13 Utes win.

Other than a Houston rout of Southern, where he left the game early, Weigman hasn't been below 200 yards. Be it injury or game situation, Weigman hasn't run as much this season. Last year, he had over 100 yards rushing in three different games. If UC can keep the passing yards down, the Cougars may have to run. Against Utah, Houston only had 86 rushing yards.

Life at leading 24-6 (vs. No. 8 Texas Tech) is a lot easier than trailing 42-6 (vs. then-No. 6 Utah). Particularly on the road, a halftime lead can be a spark. In their five wins, UC led in three games at the half (Boston College, Western Carolina, Texas Tech). Against Miami University and Kansas State, UC trailed and came back in Cincinnati.

Houston has only trailed at halftime once this season, a 10-0 deficit at UCF on Oct. 3. They stormed back to win 27-17.

Winning on the Big 12 road is not easy. The Bearcats won at Kansas and Oklahoma State in 2025, at UCF in 2024, and recorded their first Big 12 win in Houston three years ago.

"They played Utah last week and the week before they played Texas Tech and really got after 'em," Fritz told the Houston media. "They're a good squad: offense, defense, kicking game. I wouldn't say they're built the same as us, but they've done a really nice job in the portal."

"Physical runner. Same thing with us, it starts with their offensive line. We've got one of the highest-ranked offensive lines in the Big 12, and they're right there with us. Their backs run extremely hard, and their quarterback (JC French) will play 11-on-11 football with you and run. He's going to be a threat as well."

Caught in the frenzy of the win over No. 8 Texas Tech, we horribly miscalculated the Utah game. The Utes led 42-6 at halftime on their way to a 49-25 blowout.

In my preseason predictions, this was a 31-25 loss to the Cougars based on Weigman and the lack of success in November. Updating that score, we'll say the Bearcats beat the spread, but the Cougars win 35-25.

#2827. Doc Rivers talks Giannis Antetokounmpo leaving Bucks, challenges of coaching superstar

Giannis Antetokounmpo is one-of-one. He doesn't play in the style of other superstars, which makes coaching the NBA champion and two-time MVP a particular challenge.

Doc Rivers, the former Bucks coach turned NBC Sports studio host for NBA broadcasts, pulled no punches when talking about how he found it difficult to coach Antetokounmpo in an appearance on the Bill Simmons podcast.

"I liked Giannis a lot. I liked him more as a dude. He's interesting. He's not easy. He's not easy because he plays at this crazy downhill pace. He's really a difficult guy....

"He has this great passing ability, but he doesn't necessarily have this super IQ at the same time. It's really a strange thing, and he really has one way: downhill, force, force. Every play, he wants to force it. I wish he learned how to execute better. He's one of those guys... that have never needed to execute because they can do it on their own. But that doesn't help the team. And I told Giannis this, the thing he needs to still learn is the value of execution. How important it is when you're in practice and shoot-arounds to lock in on execution. And now he has a coach [Erik Spoelstra] who is as good as there is in execution."

Rivers came in at the end of Antetokounmpo's time in Milwaukee, taking over in the middle of the 2023-24 season, and the team never found a consistent identity under Rivers' leadership. Part of that was the personnel around Antetokounmpo at the time: Jrue Holiday was gone, Kris Middleton was battling injuries and not the same player as his peak, and Damian Lillard was supposed to be the "fix."

Rivers also was there for Antetokounmpo's exit from Milwaukee, and he talked about that as well with Simmons.

"Giannis wanted out, but he was a Buck. And he didn't want to be the bad guy. He wanted [GM Jon Horst and owner Wes Edens] and those guys to say, 'We're trading you,' instead of him asking for a trade. To me, that was the game that was being played."

That take is not controversial, that's how pretty much everyone saw Antetokounmpo's exit from Milwaukee.

His comments on Antetokounmpo's play are going to draw pushback out of Miami.

#2825. Bold predictions as UC tries to win at No. 17 Houston Nov. 7

The latest Big 12 quarterback the Cincinnati Bearcats must face is a 6-foot-3 gunslinger from Cypress, Texas, about 30 miles from the University of Houston.

Conner Weigman is in his fifth year of football and has thrown for 2,053 yards and 20 touchdowns with just two interceptions this season. He is in his second year with Houston after playing at Texas A&M. He threw for 2,705 yards and 25 touchdowns last season, when the Cougars struggled to a 4-8 mark.

This season, Houston's third-down offensive efficiency is tops in the nation. Weigman also has 249 yards with his legs and six touchdowns.

UC quarterback JC French IV has thrown for 1,773 yards and 13 touchdowns with only three interceptions. A year ago, he threw for more yards than Weigman with 2,929 at Georgia Southern.

UC Bearcats football Overreactions, extended grades from UC Bearcats vs. No. 6 Utah Utes

French is heading toward career-highs on the ground. For UC to be successful against Houston's high-powered offense, they will likely need another successful day running the football and an error-free day in the air.

Defensively, the Bearcats have to keep Houston below their averages of 36 points and 470 total offensive yards.

"I think first down will be critical this week against Houston," UC head coach Scott Satterfield said. "They're so efficient. They don't have many negative plays. If we can try to knock them off a little on first down, it will make that third down a little bit longer. These offenses, when it's third and three or four or less, they can do everything. It makes it a lot more difficult to stop them. If you get them in that long-yardage scenario, you get a better idea of how to get them off the field."

Cole Tabb did have 131 yards vs. Utah, and Gi'Bran Payne had 67. In four of their five wins, UC has had over 250 rushing yards. A healthy Payne should help, as well as anything either can offer in the passing game.

Utah ran for 226 yards against Houston in their most recent game Oct. 24, a 21-13 Utes win.

Other than a Houston rout of Southern, where he left the game early, Weigman hasn't been below 200 yards. Be it injury or game situation, Weigman hasn't run as much this season. Last year, he had over 100 yards rushing in three different games. If UC can keep the passing yards down, the Cougars may have to run. Against Utah, Houston only had 86 rushing yards.

Life at leading 24-6 (vs. No. 8 Texas Tech) is a lot easier than trailing 42-6 (vs. then-No. 6 Utah). Particularly on the road, a halftime lead can be a spark. In their five wins, UC led in three games at the half (Boston College, Western Carolina, Texas Tech). Against Miami University and Kansas State, UC trailed and came back in Cincinnati.

Houston has only trailed at halftime once this season, a 10-0 deficit at UCF on Oct. 3. They stormed back to win 27-17.

Winning on the Big 12 road is not easy. The Bearcats won at Kansas and Oklahoma State in 2025, at UCF in 2024, and recorded their first Big 12 win in Houston three years ago.

"They played Utah last week and the week before they played Texas Tech and really got after 'em," Fritz told the Houston media. "They're a good squad: offense, defense, kicking game. I wouldn't say they're built the same as us, but they've done a really nice job in the portal."

"Physical runner. Same thing with us, it starts with their offensive line. We've got one of the highest-ranked offensive lines in the Big 12, and they're right there with us. Their backs run extremely hard, and their quarterback (JC French) will play 11-on-11 football with you and run. He's going to be a threat as well."

Caught in the frenzy of the win over No. 8 Texas Tech, we horribly miscalculated the Utah game. The Utes led 42-6 at halftime on their way to a 49-25 blowout.

In my preseason predictions, this was a 31-25 loss to the Cougars based on Weigman and the lack of success in November. Updating that score, we'll say the Bearcats beat the spread, but the Cougars win 35-25.

#2824. 2026-27 NHL season predictions: Expert picks for Stanley Cup playoffs, champion and major awards this season

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Following a brief offseason and an expedited preseason, the 2026-27 NHL season has arrived. Before the puck drops on opening night, we have some predictions to make.

If this season feel like it's staring earlier than usual, that's because it is. The NHL is adopting an 84-game regular season, which just means more hockey for the rest of us. That also means a long and arduous journey to the Stanley Cup is ever so slightly more difficult.

So, what will that journey look like? The Carolina Hurricanes are looking to defend their title as Cup champions, but they'll have to contend with a deep Eastern Conference and some real juggernauts in the Western Conference. With that in mind, we logged our expert predictions for the playoff field in each conference -- and there were a few surprises -- before making our Stanley Cup Final selections.

We also called our shot on the winners of each major individual award. Connor McDavid is looking for his fourth Hart Trophy, but he's got some competition from an up-and-coming superstar in his own division. Races for the Norris Trophy and Vezina Trophy should be pretty wide open, and unexpected candidates always emerge throughout the season.

It should be a fun season in the NHL, so follow along with all our coverage at CBS Sports. Let's get things kicked off with the season preview and predictions, which will of course be 100% accurate.

Baumgartner: I don't see many new faces entering the conversation when it comes to the Eastern Conference playoff race. A healthy Florida Panthers side will slot themselves right back towards the top of the Atlantic, and a revamped Washington Capitals side should be able to make some noise in the Metropolitan. Besides that, I have six 2026 playoff teams returning to the dance in 2027.

Nivison: As much as I hate to go with chalk in preseason predictions -- because it rarely happens that way -- there's no denying the top dogs in the West. The Avalanche and Stars are the class of the Central Division, and the Golden Knights should pound a pitiful Pacific Division into a pulp. Things get more interesting behind those clear Cup contenders, and I'm projecting another significant leap forward from the Mammoth. I also think Macklin Celebrini will be successful in dragging the Sharks to the playoffs in his third NHL season.

Nivison -- Columbus Blue Jackets: The Blue Jackets have been agonizingly close to the playoffs in each of the last two seasons, and I think they get over the hump in 2026-27. There are still questions in Columbus. Can Adam Fantilli be a franchise player at center? Is the forward group as a whole good enough to keep pace in a competitive Eastern Conference? Still, I am sure the Blue Jackets have a really strong blue line, led by Norris Trophy winner Zach Werenski, and goaltender Jet Greaves is on track to become a Vezina Trophy candidate. Internal improvements from the young core will then get Columbus above the cut line.

Baumgartner -- San Jose Sharks: The Sharks narrowly missed out on the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, finishing just four points short of the second wild card. San Jose added a good group of veterans over the summer, but the most important offseason move was selecting Ivar Stenberg with the No. 2 pick in the Draft. Stenberg joins the youth movement in San Jose, which is spearheaded by new captain Macklin Celebrini, who broke the Sharks single-season points record with 115 last season. The Sharks are a better team than they were last year, and with Celebrini entering his third season as a legit Hart Trophy contender, this team won't be fun to play against.

Nivison: Yes, the Mammoth have a brutal path coming out of the Central Divison, but just close your eyes and imagine this scenario with me. Logan Cooley becomes a superstar center. Dylan Guenther hits 50 goals. Dmitry Simashev asserts himself as a budding top-four defenseman. Anders Lee and Vincent Trocheck provide necessary veteran depth. Now open your eyes. Utah is your Western Conference champion.

Unfortunately for the Mammoth, they will run into a refreshed Panthers team that now has double-barreled Tkachuks. Last season, we found out that all it takes to stop Florida is to hope all of its key players miss significant time with injury. The long offseason was probably a blessing in disguise as it allowed the Panthers to get healthy, and that's bad news for everyone else. The structure in front of the crease will limit some of the volatility we saw from Jacob Markstrom in New Jersey, and Florida wins its third Stanley Cup in four years.

Baumgartner: Before last season, the Carolina Hurricanes' kryptonite was the Eastern Conference Final. The Hurricanes were able to overcome their demons and win the East before ultimately taking home the franchise's first Stanley Cup since 2006. In the West, the Dallas Stars have been running into the same problem. After three straight seasons ending in the Western Conference Final, the Stars regressed last postseason, flaming out in the first-round to the Minnesota Wild. The Central Division will once again be a gauntlet, but I'm ready for Dallas to take the next step and reach the Stanley Cup Final.

While Dallas has continued to fall short in recent years, the Panthers have done the opposite. The Panthers made three consecutive Stanley Cup Final appearances, winning back-to-back Cups in 2023-24 and 2024-25. Last season, Florida's three-peat attempt came to a halt on day one of training after captain Aleksander Barkov went down with a non-contact injury, tearing both the ACL and MCL in his right knee. An offseason of healing for Barkov, and the rest of the banged up Panthers, has the team refreshed entering September for the first time in years. With nearly the entire 2025 Stanley Cup winning core still on the team and Brady Tkachuk added to the fold, Florida looks ready to win its third Stanley Cup in four seasons.

Nivison: Celebrini should have won the Hart Trophy last season, but for some incomprehensible reason, he wasn't even a finalist. This year, Celebrini replicates that performance and gets San Jose to the postseason to take home his first MVP award at age 20. Hughes posts a career year in his first full season with the Wild, and Spencer Carberry gets his flowers for winning the Metro Division after missing the playoffs last year.

Baumgartner: McDavid's ability to take over a game was evident nearly every time he touched the ice last season. His 24 points (11 goals,13 assists) in the final 14 games of the regular season -- without Leon Draisaitl in the lineup -- was one of the many reasons I put him No. 1 on my Hart Trophy ballot. With just two years left on his current contract, desperation may start to kick in to get the job in Edmonton, which would lead to another MVP-caliber season. Barkov is healthy and the frontrunner to win his fourth Selke, and Dahlin will have another strong season to take home his first career Norris Trophy.

#2821. Xavier advances to state volleyball title match, Kimberly falls in semifinal

ASHWAUBENON – Xavier will play for the WIAA Division 2 state girls volleyball championship on Saturday, Nov. 7, at the Resch Center.

Kimberly wasn't as fortunate in Division 1.

Xavier, the No. 1 seed, advanced to the D2 title match with a 25-16, 25-23, 15-25, 25-19 victory over No. 4 seed Catholic Memorial on Nov. 6 in a semifinal match.

The Hawks (30-11) will play No. 2 seed Kettle Moraine Lutheran (31-10) in the championship match at 5 p.m. Saturday. The Chargers advanced with a 27-25, 23-25, 25-21, 25-23 victory over Barron.

Kimberly, the No. 2 seed, was swept in its Division 1 semifinal by No. 3 seed Bay Port 25-22, 25-16, 25-12 to end the season for the Papermakers.

Bay Port will play in the championship match Saturday at 7:30 p.m. against No. 1 seed Divine Savior Holy Angels, which advanced with a 21-25, 25-22, 25-18, 25-14 victory over Wisconsin Lutheran.

Xavier is no stranger to the state tournament – it won Division 2 state titles as recently as 2022 and 2023 – but the postseason run is a new experience for this group and they're cherishing it.

"We are incredibly blessed," Xavier coach Luke Herriges said. "That was a phenomenal volleyball match playing against Catholic Memorial, who is one of the best teams that we've played this year, especially defensively and at the net. They play some power volleyball. They were frustrating at times at how much they would dig and block us.

"But our kids found a way, and I think that's just the story of this whole entire year is that they found the way to persevere with challenges. We're incredibly excited to play for a state championship tomorrow and couldn't be happier."

The Hawks never trailed in the first two sets. The first set was tied 8-8 and the second set was tied 5-5 before the Hawks pulled away in both.

The Crusaders scored the first point in the third set to lead for the first time in the match and controlled the third set, but the Hawks took back the momentum of the match in the fourth set and went on to the victory.

"Hats off to Xavier. They came out and battled. They executed really well. They were scrappy the whole match," CMH coach Samantha Derynda said. "We had a lot of power. I think we just started off a little bit scared and got behind in set one and two, and then it kind of hurt us. Set three, we just showed who we were, right? Unfortunately, we couldn't get enough to make it happen through the fourth set."

Rose Kendall had 14 kills for Xavier. Raya Zurfluh had 34 assists, while Hope Kaufman had 19 digs, Zurfluh had 15 digs and Taelyn Kiepert had 13 digs.

Kendall said the Hawks being able to turn back the CMH momentum after that third set was crucial.

"I think one thing we really focus on is holding the huddles tight, knowing that the set isn't over until, you know, it hits 25 or whatever the score is," Kendall said. "And I think in that moment, we've really talked about embracing everything that's happening. The game isn't going our way every time, but we stick together and we know that we're going to do this together."

Xavier was going to relax the rest of the day Friday and prepare to face a Kettle Moraine Lutheran team that the Hawks beat 2-1 at the Homestead Joust earlier this season.

"The message is to enjoy your last day with this team, to enjoy everything from the bus ride to the dances in the locker room, to just go up there and have a blast with your friends, because it'll never be the same," Herriges said.

Kimberly didn't have an answer for the hitting prowess of Bay Port, led by senior outside hitter Brenna Derousseau who had 23 kills.

The Pirates had 46 kills in the match and a .343 hitting percentage, while Kimberly had 26 kills and a .100 hitting percentage.

"Tons of credit to Bay Port. They were definitely ready," Kimberly coach Carrie Raminger said. "I felt like it was similar to how teams have felt this season playing us. There were a lot of options and they definitely worked our block harder than they've had to work in a while. And I think that you saw that, and then defensively you saw some frustration because their outsides were able to move the ball around in a lot of different spots."

Harper Van Lannen had eight kills for Kimberly. Aubrey Van Camp had 18 assists and Finley Van Lannen had 19 digs.

Harper Van Lannen said the Papermakers weren't surprised by how well Bay Port played. Kimberly beat the Pirates 2-0 at the Notre Dame Invite early in the season.

"I think we go into every game expecting other people's best," she said. "I feel like we've talked about how everyone is going to play their best against us, so we have to be ready for that. So I don't think it really surprised us. I just think that we just weren't playing as a team today."

Kimberly has a young roster and says goodbye to only four seniors – the Van Lannens, Haylie Dulas and Kylie Ver Bockel.

The Papermakers were playing at the state tournament for the second year in a row and for the 14th time overall and expectations continue to grow for the program.

They finished the season with a 38-5 record.

"It is an expectation to get here, but we also know how hard it is to get here," Raminger said. "Throughout our whole season, we have felt a little bit of pressure and we have done a really good job of fighting it off, fighting it off, and staying grounded in the things that we know.

"We haven't always won. We have been in that spot where we didn't. And so we have been battle-tested and today, unfortunately, you didn't see our best, but that doesn't take away from how cool the season has been and how fun it has been to coach them and the rest of the senior class."

#2819. Giannis Antetokounmpo is ‘difficult’ to coach: Doc Rivers

Retired NBA coach Doc Rivers is never afraid to speak the truth, and Giannis Antetokounmpo is on his mind these days.

Rivers explained on the "Bill Simmons Podcast" that Antetokounmpo is a "difficult guy" after having coached him for a season and a half before retiring in April 2026.

"He's not easy," Rivers said of coaching Antetokounmpo. "He plays at this crazy downhill pace. He's really a difficult guy. He has this great passing ability, but he doesn't have super IQ at the same time. He really has one way. Every play, he wants to force it."

Giannis Antetokounmpo of the Miami Heat shoots a free throw during a game against the Golden State Warriors in San Francisco on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images

Antetokounmpo is an ultra-rare physical specimen, earning the nickname "The Greek Freak," standing 6-foot-11 and weighing 250 pounds.

His time in Milwaukee is mostly considered a success, as he won an NBA title in 2021, but the end of his career with Rivers was frustrating. The Bucks had nearly no assets to acquire new players and Antetokounmpo himself was a constant source of trade conjecture.

"I wished he learned how to execute better," Rivers said. "The thing he needs to still learn is the value of execution. How important it is when you're in practice and shoot around to lock in on execution. Now he has a coach who's as good as there is in execution."

The Bucks finally did trade him to the Miami Heat this past offseason and he's hooked up with coach Erik Spoelstra, though early returns have not been good with a 3-6 record.

"For the team to work, you have to learn how to execute," Rivers said.

Rivers has always been honest when talking about players he's coaching, including when he's still with the team.

Head coach Doc Rivers and Giannis Antetokounmpo #34 of the Milwaukee Bucks look on against the Brooklyn Nets during the game at Barclays Center on December 08, 2024 in New York Getty Images

As the 76ers coach, Rivers had a blunt answer to a reporter after Ben Simmons passed up a wide-open layup in Game 7 of a playoff game against the Atlanta Hawks in 2021.

The reporter asked whether Rivers still believed in Simmons to be an elite point guard on a championship-winning team.

"I don't know that question or the answer to that right now," Rivers replied after they lost to a clearly inferior Hawks team that went on to not be a contender in the years following. "So I don't know the answer to that."

Simmons refused to show up the following year and was eventually traded to the Nets for James Harden before falling out of the league in a detrimental chain of events for his career.

Simmons later said Rivers' comments infuriated him.

Doc Rivers has never been one to clam up when talking about his players. USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con

"How did I feel? I was like, 'What a piece of s—t," Simmons said of Rivers' blunt comments in a recent documentary "Ben Being Ben". "When times get tough, people start panicking. People throw people under the bus, and that's just what happened."

Antetokounmpo and the Heat face the floundering Kings on Sunday after losing to the Warriors on Thursday.

#2818. Chargers-Texans Game Preview: Can 2 returning starters on offense make the difference?

The Chargers are back inside SoFi Stadium to face the Texans (2-5) this Sunday.

It's been hell for Justin Herbert and the offense all year, but it's been just as rough when they've played the Texans each of the past two seasons. Houston has picked off Herbert five times and chances are they'll add to that total this weekend given how things have gone for two months of the season now.

Can they FINALLY shock the fan base and dig out their first win? Will the woes continue against Houston? I guess we have to tune in to find out.

Here are the three things I'll be watching the closest when these two teams take the field on Sunday.

The Chargers offense will hopefully look a bit different this week with a pair starters returning to the fold.

Tight end David Njoku had his activation window opened this week and has logged a pair of limited practices this week. He was one of Justin Herbert's top targets through the team's first two games and I'll be interested to see if that continues once he's back.

Kayode Awosika, the team's starting left guard to begin the season, also looks to be making his way back to the field after a pair of limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Awosika was one of the offensive line's best performance before going down with a fibula injury and I wouldn't be shocked if his presence next to Joe Alt on the left side moves the needle — in some way at least — on offense this week.

Njoky being a pass-catching tight end first and forement could help the passing game while Awosika's return could potentially open up things on the ground. Now of course one player in each facet likely isn't enough to be a true fix, but that unit needs anything at all and two former starters returning to the field is a good start.

The last two times Justin Herbert and the Chargers have faced the Texans have been a nightmare.

In last year's matchup on December 25th, the Chargers lost 20-16 in a game Herbert threw one touchdown to one interception. The prior game against Houston was the wild card matchup in January of '25 where Herbert threw four interceptions in one of his worst outings as a pro.

As much as I wish I could say this is a real opportunity to exorcise the demons from those two games, I simply cannot. Herbert and the Chargers have never looked like a worse, less-cohesive unit and even with the Houston defense not its usual elite self, they still have numerous players who can make a splash play at a moment's notice.

Even the return of a healthy Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston, and Tre' Harris did next to nothing for the offense's production in Week Eight. Coming out of the bye, the Chargers scored just nine points, all of which came in the first half. They were then completely blanked in the second as Herbert threw his second interception on top of nearly losing a fumble that was luckily knocked out of bounds.

At this rate, nothing is going to come to save the Chargers from themselves. If they want the nightmare to end, they've gotta wake up and do it themselves.

Stroud did not have to play at an All-Pro or Pro Bowl level the past two seasons while the Texans defense was arguably the best in the league from 2024-2025. This year, with the defense taking some steps back, he's had to carry the load a bit more and that's somewhat worked out after a rough start. The Texans are the NFL's 7th-ranked passing offense and that is mainly due to an abysmal run game averaging only 84.7 yards per game (29th).

After throwing for at least 260 yards in Weeks Four through Six (including two games of over 300), Stroud only threw for 153 in their loss to the Giants just before their bye. With two weeks of preparation, you have to think they'll be ready to roll.

On the flip side, the Chargers pass defense currently ranks 7th in the league, as well (198.4). That rank has mostly been maintained without All-Pro safety Derwin James or veteran cornerback Donte Jackson in the lineup. If that's not the far-and-away strength of the Bolts defense, then I don't know what is. Just a bunch of names putting together a top-10 unit under a first-year defensive coordinator.

#2813. Report: Warriors expected to trade Kristaps Porzingis by December 16th

The Golden State Warriors Kristaps Porzingis saga is expected to come to an end before the end of the year, according to a report by Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints. Porzingis, who re-signed with the Dubs last season on a partially guaranteed two-year, $40 million deal, opted not to join the team for training camp and has accepted not receiving payments, seemingly deciding to retire. However, hoping to make the best out of an unexpected situation, the Warriors are hoping to use Porzingis' salary essentially as a trade exception. While that was all known, Siegel's reporting suggests the front office is expected to trade Porzingis by December 16th.

"For starters, Porzingis' time with the Warriors is over," Siegel wrote. "He will not be playing another game for this franchise, as ClutchPoints reported on Oct. 23 before the team's first game of the season, and it's almost a given he will be traded, likely within the next 30-40 days… Much like how the Warriors traded for Dennis Schroder in the middle of December during the 2024-25 season, only to re-aggregate him in a bigger deal for Jimmy Butler at the trade deadline, league sources are anticipating a similar strategy this time around with Porzingis."

Siegel notes that players who signed free agent contracts this offseason will all become trade-eligible on December 15th, which will also give teams more options on that day. Moreover, December 16th is the deadline for a player to be traded and still be eligible to be aggregated in a deal at the trade deadline in February. So while it's definitely possible for a deal to be made sooner, that effectively becomes the deadline for the Warriors front office if they would like to make a smaller move with Porzingis that would leave them flexibility to still go looking for bigger fish at the deadline.

Siegel's reporting does not even engage with a scenario where the Warriors do not trade Porzingis in December. It's worth wondering if they would simply hold onto him until the trade deadline if they did not receive an offer that enticed them enough before. With the Warriors 6-3 and looking like a legit playoff team, though, the front office should be less inclined to slow play adding depth to the roster.

#2811. Freiburg end Thomas Reis’ winning streak at Trabzonspor by stopping Salah in battling away victory

SC Freiburg earned a hard-fought win in their UEFA Europa Conference League trip to Trabzonspor. Julian Schuster's side are now level on points with their hosts after ending Thomas Reis’ seven-game winning start at the Turkish side.

Despite the electric atmosphere from the home fans, Freiburg were calm in possession from the first whistle. They thoroughly deserved the opening goal that arrived in the 14th minute from a set-piece opportunity.

André Onana saved Igor Matanović's powerful header from Vincenzo Grifo's corner-kick delivery, but the rebound fell kindly to Lukas Kübler as the all-rounder scored his fifth European goal with a simple finish.

The Cameroonian goalkeeper was at fault for Freiburg's next chance, although Matanović left him off the hook with a weak effort. Trabzonspor had the first real chance with Ernest Muçi's effort from outside the box moments after Mohamed Salah's deflected free-kick.

Freiburg threatened to double their lead from set-piece situations as Batista Mendy made a crucial block to deny the captain Maximilian Eggestein before Onana dealt with Grifo's direct free-kick. Salah had his first open play chance before the half-time break, but his effort was wide off the mark. At the other end, Grifo's customary shot similarly failed to hit the target before Cyriaque Irié's unsuccessful header.

The home fans put the referee Kristo Tohvar under pressure early after the restart as he waved play to continue following an incident inside Freiburg's box involving Paul Onuachu and Kübler. The Nigerian striker then created a big chance for Salah, but Mio Backhaus made his first big save from close range.

For the first time in the game, the Bundesliga side were under immense pressure with all the action restricted to one half of the pitch. However, they managed to weather Trabzon's second-half storm as Backhaus and his defenders dealt with several crosses into the box. Thanks to their first clean sheet since matchday 3 in Bundesliga, last season's Europa League finalists have now won three consecutive games in different competitions.

Freiburg will host Union Berlin before the international break as they hope to stay in the top three of the Bundesliga. Their remaining Europa Conference League games will see them face Twente (H), Panathinaikos (H) and Kauno Zalgiris (A).

#2800. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2799. Walker Kessler is having more of an impact than it looks

Since the Lakers acquired Walker Kessler over the summer, most of the conversation regarding his play, and subsequent impact, has been tied to the cost paid to land him.

The multiple years and millions of dollars, the draft picks and swaps, each have served as footnotes after every game thus far.

While fair given what the Lakers need from him going forward, it has also put increased emphasis on his raw production rather than influence. If you're into that kind of thing, Kessler's per-game numbers are solid. His 14.4 points, 10.2 rebounds and four stocks nightly will play. However, it doesn't capture the full spectrum of his impact.

On offense, Kessler is still navigating life as Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves' screener. It's an entirely new world compared to the barren guard groups he played next to with the Utah Jazz.

Things like timing, pick angles and court-mapping will take time. But the early results have been encouraging nevertheless.

After his dunk-centric eruption on opening night, defenses have already begun selling out in the paint to take away his lob and cut chances.

Due to this, Kessler has not been able to duplicate his scoring outbursts, but it hasn't lessened his value to the offense either. A direct result of teams loading up and tagging Kessler — often with multiple defenders — is that it has created open shots from the perimeter, as seen in the clips below.

Kessler's roll gravity also extends to his rebounding ability. As one of the league's best second-chance creators, and simply being a massive person, Kessler often draws multiple players to him whenever a shot goes up.

This fear is well warranted. The Lakers' offensive rebound percentage jolts up nearly 10% when Kessler is on the floor compared to off. Like a black hole, this sucks up defenders from the corners and creates quality looks for shooters. The Lakers are currently shooting 43.9% from the corners this season, the second-best mark in the league.

Beyond the attention Kessler attracts on offense simply from existing, his omnipresence is probably best demonstrated with the impact he's had on the Lakers' defense.

As the backbone and backline, Kessler's presence in the paint has allowed the team's wings to be extremely aggressive shocking the ball with the trust that the center will clean up any mistakes. This disruptive style has resulted in the Lakers being one of the best defenses in terms of forced turnovers.

And when his teammates do get burned for gambling or getting blown by, Kessler has been iron-clad protecting the basket.

Not only are opposing teams shooting just 26.9% of their shots at the rim when Kessler is on the floor — would rank fourth-best in the NBA — they are also missing once he meets them there.

Among the 12 players who have defended at least 50 shots within six feet this season, Kessler ranks first in defended shooting percentage against (45.1%) while also contesting the second-most attempts behind only Victor Wembanyama, according to the league's tracking data.

Kessler's deterrence and effectiveness in shutting off the paint is not solely due to his size.

His height and frightening wingspan do help, yes. But what drives his success is his impressive motor. With every second jump contest, race down the floor and closeout to a 3-point shooter, Kessler's care factor is never in doubt. That goes a long way to actualizing his defensive upside.

Despite how hard he ultimately tries, the Lakers are learning firsthand that Kessler can't be everywhere at once. This is never more true than the defensive drop-off once he's on the bench.

Through their first nine games, the Lakers have allowed a defensive rating of 110.1 with Kessler on the court compared to 117.2 when he's been off. That's a discrepancy that is the equivalent of the team performing like the eighth-best defense versus the 26th.

While his individual numbers will likely fluctuate nightly, and even quarterly, as illustrated by his dominant final frame — 10 points, five rebounds, four blocks and a steal — against the Sacramento Kings on Wednesday, Kessler has proven to be more than suited for the role bestowed upon him.

He may not be the thundering force that Dončić is or as crafty as Reaves, but Kessler's job as the Lakers' silent protector has been as critical to the team's strong start.

It won't always look like he's had a good game in the box score. But just watch how that opposing ball-handler goes wide-eyed and makes a U-turn when the giant in purple and gold makes his stand.

More than any numbers can ever quantify, Kessler's game is measured in fear. And the Lakers are benefiting from it so far.
